Also: no compliance needed for non-professional or scientific research use (these persons are 'encouraged to voluntarily comply'); simplified compliance for SMEs. Could bear on public bodies that fine-tune models [inference]. Nearest named actor: whoever modifies or fine-tunes a model.
Note (B): Relevant where a public body fine-tunes a model [inference]. Also: non-professional or scientific research users excluded but 'encouraged to voluntarily comply'; simplified compliance for SMEs.

Quote (A): there should be a possibility for the Commission to take individual decisions designating a general-purpose AI model as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk if it is found that such model has capabilities or an impact equivalent
Quote (B): there should be a possibility for the Commission to take individual decisions designating a general-purpose AI model as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'there should be a possibility'); describes a designation power
Note (A): Complements a FLOPs threshold that creates a presumption of systemic risk; the threshold 'should be adjusted over time' and supplemented with benchmarks. The decision rests on annex criteria (data size, number of users, modalities, autonomy, tools). Recital (113): the Commission 'should be empowered to designate' where the provider failed to notify. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (reassessment on request, Recital 111).
Note (B): Based on annex criteria (training data, users, modalities, autonomy, tools). An 'initial threshold of floating point operations should be set' and 'adjusted over time' (holder not stated). Recital (113): Commission 'should be empowered to designate' where the provider failed to notify.

Quote (A): To inform this, the AI Office should engage with the scientific community, industry, civil society and other experts.
Quote (B): To inform this, the AI Office should engage with the scientific community, industry, civil society and other experts.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office, within the Commission)
Note (A): Engagement to inform the threshold and the benchmarks and indicators for model capability.
Note (B): Engagement to inform thresholds, benchmarks and indicators.

Quote (A): Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk, the Commission should take the request into account and may decide to reassess
Quote (B): Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk, the Commission should take the request into account and may decide to reassess
Holder (A): the Commission (on a reasoned request of a provider)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should take the request into account and may decide')
Note (A): Challenge route for designated providers: the Commission answers the request; reassessment is discretionary ('may').
Note (B): Challenge/review route for providers against a designation.

Quote (A): The provider should notify the AI Office at the latest two weeks after the requirements are met or it becomes known that a general-purpose AI model will meet the requirements that lead to the presumption.
Quote (B): The provider should notify the AI Office at the latest two weeks after the requirements are met or it becomes known that a general-purpose AI model will meet the requirements that lead to the presumption.
Holder (A): The provider (of a general-purpose AI model meeting the threshold)
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
If not met (A): not stated here (Recital 113: the Commission may designate the model where the provider failed to notify)
Note (A): Reports to: the AI Office. In the notification the provider 'should be able to demonstrate' that the model exceptionally does not present systemic risks. Trigger: threshold met or foreseeably met (can be before training is complete).
Note (B): Trigger: threshold met or foreseeable. Provider may argue its model 'exceptionally does not present systemic risks'. Reporting to the regulator; also a Coordination link.

Quote (A): A system of qualified alerts should ensure that the AI Office is made aware by the scientific panel of general-purpose AI models that should possibly be classified as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
Quote (B): A system of qualified alerts should ensure that the AI Office is made aware by the scientific panel of general-purpose AI models that should possibly be classified as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
Holder (A): the scientific panel; the AI Office
Holder (B): the scientific panel; the AI Office
Position (A): EU expert body (independent experts) and public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Alert mechanism from the scientific panel to the AI Office, alongside the AI Office's own monitoring.
Note (B): Alert channel from scientific panel to AI Office, in addition to AI Office monitoring.

Quote (A): this Regulation should require providers to perform the necessary model evaluations, in particular prior to its first placing on the market, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of models, also, as appropriate, through internal or independent external testing.
Quote (B): this Regulation should require providers to perform the necessary model evaluations, in particular prior to its first placing on the market, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of models, also, as appropriate, through internal or independent external testing
Holder (A): providers of general-purpose AI models presenting systemic risks
Holder (B): providers of general-purpose AI models presenting systemic risks
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
Note (A): Model evaluation and adversarial testing. Trigger: in particular before first placing on the market; compared against: systemic risks; metric: not stated. Applies whether the model is standalone or embedded in a system or product.
Note (B): Trigger: before first placing on market. Check: model evaluations and adversarial testing, internal or independent external. Compares against: not stated. Metric: not stated.

Quote (A): providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks should continuously assess and mitigate systemic risks, including for example by putting in place risk-management policies, such as accountability and governance processes, implementing post-market monitoring
Quote (B): providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks should continuously assess and mitigate systemic risks, including for example by putting in place risk-management policies, such as accountability and governance processes, implementing post-market monitoring
Holder (A): providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
Holder (B): providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
Note (A): Ongoing risk assessment, mitigation and post-market monitoring 'along the entire model’s lifecycle', and 'cooperating with relevant actors along the AI value chain'. Trigger: continuous.
Note (B): Ongoing. Also 'cooperating with relevant actors along the AI value chain' (Coordination).

Quote (A): the general-purpose AI model provider should without undue delay keep track of the incident and report any relevant information and possible corrective measures to the Commission and national competent authorities.
Quote (B): the general-purpose AI model provider should without undue delay keep track of the incident and report any relevant information and possible corrective measures to the Commission and national competent authorities
Holder (A): the general-purpose AI model provider (with systemic risk)
Holder (B): the general-purpose AI model provider (with systemic risk)
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
Note (A): Serious-incident reporting. Answers to: the Commission and national competent authorities; consequence: not stated. Trigger: a serious incident caused by development or use of the model.
Note (B): Trigger: serious incident from development or use of the model. Answer to: Commission and national competent authorities.

Quote (A): providers should ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure, if appropriate, along the entire model lifecycle.
Quote (B): providers should ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure, if appropriate, along the entire model lifecycle
Holder (A): providers (of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk)
Holder (B): providers (of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks)
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
Note (A): Covers accidental model leakage, unauthorised releases, circumvention of safety measures, cyberattacks, unauthorised access and model theft; e.g. securing model weights.
Note (B): Covers model leakage, unauthorised release, circumvention of safety measures, model theft; e.g. securing model weights.

Quote (A): The AI Office should encourage and facilitate the drawing up, review and adaptation of codes of practice, taking into account international approaches.
Quote (B): The AI Office should encourage and facilitate the drawing up, review and adaptation of codes of practice, taking into account international approaches.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office, within the Commission)
Note (A): Codes of practice for general-purpose AI model providers. The AI Office 'should collaborate with relevant national competent authorities' and 'could' consult civil society, experts and the Scientific Panel; all GPAI providers 'could be invited to participate'. Codes should cover a systemic-risk taxonomy and risk assessment and mitigation measures. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (approval, Recital 117).
Note (B): Facilitation, not authority, so coded Coordination. All GPAI providers 'could be invited to participate'; AI Office 'should collaborate with relevant national competent authorities, and could ... consult with civil society organisations ... including the Scientific Panel'. Codes should cover GPAI obligations, a Union-level systemic-risk taxonomy and risk assessment/mitigation measures.

Quote (A): By means of implementing acts, the Commission may decide to approve a code of practice and give it a general validity within the Union, or, alternatively, to provide common rules for the implementation of the relevant obligations
Quote (B): By means of implementing acts, the Commission may decide to approve a code of practice and give it a general validity within the Union, or, alternatively, to provide common rules for the implementation of the relevant obligations
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'may decide'); describes an implementing power
Note (A): Standard-setting for GPAI providers. Common rules apply if a code 'cannot be finalised or is not deemed adequate by the AI Office'. Providers can rely on codes, or on harmonised standards assessed as suitable by the AI Office (presumption of conformity), or on 'alternative adequate means'.
Note (B): Common rules apply if a code 'cannot be finalised or is not deemed adequate by the AI Office'. Standard-setting authority.

Quote (A): the Commission should be able to establish, via implementing acts, and after consultation of the advisory forum, common specifications for certain requirements under this Regulation.
Quote (B): the Commission should be able to establish, via implementing acts, and after consultation of the advisory forum, common specifications for certain requirements under this Regulation
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be able to'); describes an implementing power
Note (A): Fallback standard-setting when harmonised standards are absent, rejected, delayed, non-compliant with the request, or 'insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns'. The Commission 'is encouraged to cooperate with international partners and international standardisation bodies'.
Note (B): Fall-back where standards are not accepted, 'insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns', do not comply with the request, or are delayed. Also: 'the standardisation requests should be issued by the Commission without undue delay', consulting the advisory forum and the Board.

Quote (A): the conformity assessment of such systems should be carried out as a general rule by the provider under its own responsibility, with the only exception of AI systems intended to be used for biometrics.
Quote (B): the conformity assessment of such systems should be carried out as a general rule by the provider under its own responsibility, with the only exception of AI systems intended to be used for biometrics
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Note (A): For high-risk systems not related to products (the annex use cases, which include most public-sector uses [inference]), self-assessment by the provider; third-party assessment by notified bodies only for biometrics, 'at least in an initial phase'. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service (Recital 123).
Note (B): Self-assessment for high-risk systems not related to products (which would include most public-service use cases [inference]); third-party assessment only for biometrics, 'at least in an initial phase'.

Quote (A): notified bodies should be notified under this Regulation by the national competent authorities, provided that they comply with a set of requirements, in particular on independence, competence, absence of conflicts of interests and suitable cybersecurity requirements.
Quote (B): notified bodies should be notified under this Regulation by the national competent authorities, provided that they comply with a set of requirements, in particular on independence, competence, absence of conflicts of interests and suitable cybersecurity requirements
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority (notifying authority)
Note (A): Appointing who carries out third-party checks. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (notification tool, Recital 126).
Note (B): Appointing who carries out third-party checks; criteria: independence, competence, no conflicts of interest, cybersecurity.

Quote (A): Notification of those bodies should be sent by national competent authorities to the Commission and the other Member States by means of the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission
Quote (B): Notification of those bodies should be sent by national competent authorities to the Commission and the other Member States by means of the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission
Position (A): public authority: member-state authorities and EU institution
Note (A): Notification between authorities via a shared tool (the tool is also a resource, provided by the Commission).
Note (B): Notification between authorities. Tool also coded Coordination/Resources.

Quote (A): the Commission should actively explore possible international instruments for that purpose and in particular pursue the conclusion of mutual recognition agreements with third countries.
Quote (B): the Commission should actively explore possible international instruments for that purpose and in particular pursue the conclusion of mutual recognition agreements with third countries
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Mutual recognition of third-country conformity assessment results. Relevance to public-sector tools is indirect [inference].
Note (B): Mutual recognition of conformity assessment results from third-country bodies.

Quote (A): when the intended purpose of the system changes, that AI system should be considered to be a new AI system which should undergo a new conformity assessment
Quote (B): that AI system should be considered to be a new AI system which should undergo a new conformity assessment
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Trigger for a re-check: any change that may affect compliance (e.g. 'change of operating system or software architecture') or a change of intended purpose. Not a substantial modification: learning changes 'pre-determined by the provider and assessed at the moment of the conformity assessment'. Nearest named actor: provider.
Note (B): Trigger: on change, 'whenever a change occurs which may affect the compliance' (e.g. operating system, software architecture) or when intended purpose changes. Exception: learning changes 'pre-determined by the provider and assessed at the moment of the conformity assessment'.

Quote (A): High-risk AI systems should bear the CE marking to indicate their conformity with this Regulation so that they can move freely within the internal market.
Quote (B): High-risk AI systems should bear the CE marking to indicate their conformity with this Regulation
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Visible sign-off of conformity; a digital CE marking for systems provided only digitally. Member States 'should not create unjustified obstacles' to compliant, CE-marked systems. Nearest named actor: provider.
Note (B): Physical or digital CE marking; public signal of conformity.

Quote (A): market surveillance authorities could authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of AI systems which have not undergone a conformity assessment.
Quote (B): market surveillance authorities could authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of AI systems which have not undergone a conformity assessment
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority (market surveillance)
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'could authorise'); describes an exceptional power
Note (A): Grounds: 'exceptional reasons of public security or protection of life and health of natural persons, environmental protection and the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets'.
Note (B): Only 'under exceptional reasons of public security or protection of life and health of natural persons, environmental protection and the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets'.

Quote (A): law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation of the market surveillance authority, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay.
Quote (B): law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation of the market surveillance authority, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay
Holder (A): law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
Holder (B): law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Public-sector-specific power to deploy an unassessed high-risk system 'In duly justified situations'. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (same quote).
Note (B): Public-sector exception to the authorisation gate; the retrospective request is an accountability element.

Quote (A): should be required to register themselves and information about their AI system in an EU database, to be established and managed by the Commission.
Quote (B): should be required to register themselves and information about their AI system in an EU database, to be established and managed by the Commission
Holder (A): providers of high-risk AI systems other than those related to products falling within the scope of relevant existing Union harmonisation legislation, as well as providers who consider that an AI system listed in the high-risk use cases in an annex to this Regulation is not high-risk on the basis of a derogation
Holder (B): providers of high-risk AI systems other than those related to products under existing harmonisation legislation; providers who consider that an annex-listed AI system is not high-risk on the basis of a derogation
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Note (A): Registration. 'Any substantial modification of high-risk AI systems should also be registered'. Purpose: to 'increase the transparency towards the public'. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (database, Recital 131).
Note (B): Purpose includes 'to increase the transparency towards the public'. 'Any substantial modification of high-risk AI systems should also be registered' (trigger: on change).

Quote (A): deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies, should register themselves in such database and select the system that they envisage to use.
Quote (B): deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies, should register themselves in such database and select the system that they envisage to use
Holder (A): deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies
Holder (B): deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies
Position (A): public authority: member-state or EU public bodies
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should register'); mandatory for public-authority deployers, voluntary for other deployers ('entitled to do so voluntarily')
Note (A): Public-sector-specific registration. Trigger: 'Before using an AI system listed in the high-risk use cases in an annex'. To whom: the public, via the database (Commission controller); consequence: not stated. Law enforcement, migration, asylum and border uses go to a non-public section (next entries).
Note (B): Trigger: 'Before using an AI system listed in the high-risk use cases in an annex'. 'Other deployers should be entitled to do so voluntarily.' Public-sector-specific registration duty.

Quote (A): This section of the EU database should be publicly accessible, free of charge, the information should be easily navigable, understandable and machine-readable.
Quote (B): This section of the EU database should be publicly accessible, free of charge, the information should be easily navigable, understandable and machine-readable.
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Publication of registered information; should be 'user-friendly', with keyword search, and accessible under Directive (EU) 2019/882. Nearest named actor: the Commission (controller of the EU database).
Note (B): Publication. Nearest actor: the Commission as controller. Search functions for the public; accessibility per Directive (EU) 2019/882.

Quote (A): For high-risk AI systems in the area of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, the registration obligations should be fulfilled in a secure non-public section of the EU database.
Quote (B): For high-risk AI systems in the area of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, the registration obligations should be fulfilled in a secure non-public section of the EU database.
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be fulfilled'); exception to publication
Note (A): Reduced publicity for public-sector uses in these areas: access 'strictly limited to the Commission as well as to market surveillance authorities with regard to their national section'. Critical infrastructure systems 'should only be registered at national level'. Nearest named actors: providers and public-authority deployers in those areas.
Note (B): Public-sector carve-out from publication: 'Access to the secure non-public section should be strictly limited to the Commission as well as to market surveillance authorities with regard to their national section'. Critical-infrastructure systems 'should only be registered at national level'.

Quote (A): natural persons should be notified that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect
Quote (B): natural persons should be notified that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Disclosure to persons interacting with AI (e.g. public-facing chatbots [inference]), applying whether or not the system is high-risk, 'subject to targeted exceptions to take into account the special need of law enforcement'. Account for vulnerable groups; accessible formats. Nearest named actor: provider [inference; Art. 50 not in this part].
Note (B): Passive; recital (136) refers to 'obligations placed on providers and deployers of certain AI systems'. Applies whether or not high-risk; 'subject to targeted exceptions to take into account the special need of law enforcement'; account for vulnerable groups; accessible formats. Would cover public-service chatbots [inference].

Quote (A): natural persons should be notified when they are exposed to AI systems that, by processing their biometric data, can identify or infer the emotions or intentions of those persons or assign them to specific categories.
Quote (B): natural persons should be notified when they are exposed to AI systems that, by processing their biometric data, can identify or infer the emotions or intentions of those persons or assign them to specific categories
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Disclosure for emotion recognition and biometric categorisation; accessible formats for persons with disabilities. Nearest named actor: deployer [inference].
Note (B): Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation; information 'in accessible formats for persons with disabilities'.

Quote (A): should also clearly and distinguishably disclose that the content has been artificially created or manipulated by labelling the AI output accordingly and disclosing its artificial origin.
Quote (B): should also clearly and distinguishably disclose that the content has been artificially created or manipulated by labelling the AI output accordingly and disclosing its artificial origin
Holder (A): deployers who use an AI system to generate or manipulate image, audio or video content that appreciably resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful (deep fakes)
Holder (B): deployers who use an AI system to generate or manipulate image, audio or video content (deep fakes)
Position (A): public authority or private entity (deployer)
Note (A): Labelling of deep fakes. For evidently creative, satirical, artistic or fictional works, disclosure is limited to not hampering the work.
Note (B): Disclosure to the public; limited form for evidently creative, satirical, artistic or fictional works.

Quote (A): the Commission may also encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content
Quote (B): the Commission may also encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Including making detection mechanisms accessible and 'facilitating cooperation with other actors along the value chain, disseminating content or checking its authenticity and provenance'. EDGE CASE: supports checking whether content (including content received by public bodies) is AI-generated.
Note (B): Codes to support detection mechanisms and cooperation along the value chain, 'to enable the public to effectively distinguish AI-generated content'.

Quote (A): Member States should ensure that their national competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level to facilitate the development and testing of innovative AI systems under strict regulatory oversight
Quote (B): Member States should ensure that their national competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level to facilitate the development and testing of innovative AI systems under strict regulatory oversight
Holder (A): Member States; their national competent authorities
Holder (B): Member States; their national competent authorities
Position (A): public authority: Member States and member-state authorities
Level of obligation (A): n/a (provided); establishment described as a duty on Member States ('should ensure')
Note (A): A supervised testing environment before market or service; may be joint with other Member States, and physical, digital or hybrid. Serves testing and compliance (Delivery). Cross-ref Recitals (139)-(140).
Note (B): Testing environment before placing on market; may be joint or existing sandboxes. Serves development and testing (Delivery) under oversight.

Quote (A): Establishing authorities should also ensure that the AI regulatory sandboxes have the adequate resources for their functioning, including financial and human resources.
Quote (B): Establishing authorities should also ensure that the AI regulatory sandboxes have the adequate resources for their functioning, including financial and human resources.
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should also ensure'); required of establishing authorities
Note (A): Money and staff for sandboxes; serves the sandbox entry (Recital 138).
Note (B): Money and staff for sandboxes.

Quote (A): Any significant risks identified during the development and testing of such AI systems should result in adequate mitigation and, failing that, in the suspension of the development and testing process.
Quote (B): Any significant risks identified during the development and testing of such AI systems should result in adequate mitigation and, failing that, in the suspension of the development and testing process.
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): suspension of the development and testing process
Note (A): Authority to suspend; the holder is not named here (nearest named actors: national competent authorities supervising the sandbox).
Note (B): Pause/stop decision; nearest actor: the supervising national competent authority [inference]. Supervision covers development, training, testing, validation and substantial modification.

Quote (A): national competent authorities establishing AI regulatory sandboxes should cooperate with other relevant authorities, including those supervising the protection of fundamental rights, and could allow for the involvement of other actors within the AI ecosystem
Quote (B): national competent authorities establishing AI regulatory sandboxes should cooperate with other relevant authorities, including those supervising the protection of fundamental rights
Holder (A): national competent authorities establishing AI regulatory sandboxes
Holder (B): national competent authorities establishing AI regulatory sandboxes
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Others named: standardisation organisations, notified bodies, testing facilities, research labs, European Digital Innovation Hubs, stakeholder and civil society organisations. Common rules and 'a framework for cooperation between the relevant authorities' are to be established. Real-world testing may run inside the sandbox 'Upon agreement'.
Note (B): May involve standardisation organisations, notified bodies, testing facilities, EDIHs, stakeholder and civil society organisations; common rules and a cooperation framework between authorities supervising sandboxes; real-world testing within sandbox by agreement.

Quote (A): This Regulation should provide the legal basis for the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox to use personal data collected for other purposes for developing certain AI systems in the public interest
Quote (B): This Regulation should provide the legal basis for the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox to use personal data collected for other purposes for developing certain AI systems in the public interest
Holder (A): the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox
Holder (B): the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Level of obligation (A): n/a (provided); legal basis under specified conditions
Note (A): Data access as a resource, provided by the Regulation itself, for public-interest AI. Does not provide a basis under Art. 22(2)(b) GDPR or Art. 24(2)(b) EUDPR; other data protection duties remain.
Note (B): Data access 'only under specified conditions'; not a legal basis for solely automated decisions under Art. 22(2)(b) GDPR / Art. 24(2)(b) EUDPR.

Quote (A): require prospective providers to have a real-world testing plan submitted to competent market surveillance authority, register the testing in dedicated sections in the EU database subject to some limited exceptions
Quote (B): require prospective providers to have a real-world testing plan submitted to competent market surveillance authority, register the testing in dedicated sections in the EU database subject to some limited exceptions
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Note (A): Answers to: the market surveillance authority, plus registration. Also time limits on testing and extra safeguards for vulnerable groups.
Note (B): Answer to: market surveillance authority; registration. Also time limits and extra safeguards for vulnerable groups.

Quote (A): a written agreement defining the roles and responsibilities of prospective providers and deployers and effective oversight by competent personnel involved in the real world testing
Quote (B): a written agreement defining the roles and responsibilities of prospective providers and deployers and effective oversight by competent personnel involved in the real world testing
Position (A): public authority or private entity
Note (A): Written agreement between provider and deployer (could include public bodies hosting tests [inference]); oversight by competent personnel is also Delivery.
Note (B): Contract between provider and deployer for real-world testing; would cover public bodies as deployers [inference].

Quote (A): additional safeguards to ensure that the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded
Quote (B): additional safeguards to ensure that the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Override of AI outputs during real-world testing; personal data deleted when consent is withdrawn. Nearest named actors: prospective providers and deployers.
Note (B): Override of outputs during real-world testing. Also deletion of personal data when subjects withdraw consent.

Quote (A): the Commission should provide standardised templates for the areas covered by this Regulation, upon request of the Board.
Quote (B): the Commission should provide standardised templates for the areas covered by this Regulation, upon request of the Board
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): n/a (provided); recital 'should', on request of the Board
Note (A): Templates; framed as addressing SMEs' needs. Official offer.
Note (B): Aimed at SMEs; trigger: Board request. Serves compliance generally.

Quote (A): providing a single information platform with easy-to-use information with regards to this Regulation for all providers and deployers
Quote (B): providing a single information platform with easy-to-use information with regards to this Regulation for all providers and deployers
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Information platform for all providers and deployers (including public deployers [inference]), plus awareness campaigns. Official offer.
Note (B): Plus 'appropriate communication campaigns to raise awareness about the obligations'. Serves compliance generally, including public-authority deployers.

Quote (A): the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities established by the Commission and the Member States at Union or national level should contribute to the implementation of this Regulation.
Quote (B): the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities established by the Commission and the Member States at Union or national level should contribute to the implementation of this Regulation
Holder (A): the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities (established by the Commission and the Member States)
Holder (B): the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities (established by the Commission and the Member States)
Position (A): public authority: EU and Member State initiatives (bodies running them not specified)
Note (A): They 'are able to provide in particular technical and scientific support to providers and notified bodies'. Official offer; deployers are not named.
Note (B): Able 'to provide in particular technical and scientific support to providers and notified bodies'.

Quote (A): Member States should facilitate the tasks of the AI Office with a view to support the development of Union expertise and capabilities at Union level
Quote (B): Member States should facilitate the tasks of the AI Office with a view to support the development of Union expertise and capabilities at Union level
Position (A): public authority: Member State
Note (A): Link between Member States and the AI Office. The recital also says a Board, a scientific panel and an advisory forum 'should be established' (coded under Recitals 149-151). That the AI Office was established by Commission Decision is a report and is not coded.
Note (B): Member State to EU link.

Quote (A): The Board should be responsible for a number of advisory tasks, including issuing opinions, recommendations, advice or contributing to guidance on matters related to the implementation of this Regulation
Quote (B): The Board should be responsible for a number of advisory tasks, including issuing opinions, recommendations, advice or contributing to guidance on matters related to the implementation of this Regulation
Position (A): public authority: EU body composed of Member State representatives
Note (A): Advisory, not authority: it advises the Commission, the Member States and national competent authorities. Members are representatives from public entities 'who should have the relevant competences and powers to facilitate coordination at national level'. The Board 'should also cooperate' with Union bodies, expert groups and networks.

Quote (A): shall be deployed for the purposes set out in that point only to confirm the identity of the specifically targeted individual

Quote (A): shall be subject to a prior authorisation granted by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding of the Member State in which the use is to take place

Quote (B): Each Member State shall designate or establish at least one notifying authority responsible for setting up and carrying out the necessary procedures for the assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies and for their monitoring.
Position (A): public authority: member-state government
Note (A): Appoints who decides on designating the checkers (conformity assessment bodies). 28(2): Member States may have assessment and monitoring done by a national accreditation body under Regulation (EC) No 765/2008. Also coded Coordination/Design.
Note (B): Appointing who decides which bodies may carry out third-party conformity checks. 28(2): Member States may have a national accreditation body (Regulation (EC) No 765/2008) do the assessment and monitoring. Also coded Coordination/Design (cooperative procedures).

Quote (A): Those procedures shall be developed in cooperation between the notifying authorities of all Member States.
Quote (B): Those procedures shall be developed in cooperation between the notifying authorities of all Member States.
Holder (A): the notifying authorities of all Member States
Holder (B): the notifying authorities of all Member States
Position (A): public authority: member-state authorities
Note (A): Cross-national cooperation on designation procedures.
Note (B): Cross-Member State cooperation on notification procedures. See also Art. 38(3) (Commission-provided exchange between notifying authorities).

Quote (A): Notifying authorities shall be organised in such a way that decisions relating to the notification of conformity assessment bodies are taken by competent persons different from those who carried out the assessment of those bodies.
Quote (B): Notifying authorities shall be organised in such a way that decisions relating to the notification of conformity assessment bodies are taken by competent persons different from those who carried out the assessment of those bodies.
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Separation of assessor and decider. 28(3): no conflict of interest, objectivity and impartiality; 28(5): no CAB activities or consultancy on a commercial basis; 28(6): confidentiality (Art. 78).
Note (B): Separation of decision from assessment. 28(3): no conflict of interest with conformity assessment bodies; objectivity and impartiality. 28(5): no conformity assessment activities or commercial consultancy. 28(6): confidentiality per Art. 78.

Quote (A): Notifying authorities shall have an adequate number of competent personnel at their disposal for the proper performance of their tasks.
Quote (B): Notifying authorities shall have an adequate number of competent personnel at their disposal for the proper performance of their tasks.
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Expertise 'in fields such as information technologies, AI and law, including the supervision of fundamental rights'. Serves designation decisions (28(1)).
Note (B): Staff and expertise 'in fields such as information technologies, AI and law, including the supervision of fundamental rights'. Serves designation decisions (Art. 28(1), 30) and monitoring of notified bodies (also Accountability). Who funds it is not stated.

Quote (A): Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established.
Quote (B): Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established.
Position (A): outside the state: conformity assessment bodies [inference: usually private]
Note (A): Application includes activities, modules, AI types and accreditation certificate (29(2)) or documentary evidence (29(3)). Notified bodies update documentation 'whenever relevant changes occur' so the authority can monitor continuous compliance (29(4)). Answers to notifying authority.
Note (B): Answers to the notifying authority. Application includes activities, modules, types of AI systems, and accreditation certificate (or documentary evidence for 'verification, recognition and regular monitoring'). 29(4): notified bodies 'shall update the documentation ... whenever relevant changes occur, in order to enable the authority responsible for notified bodies to monitor and verify continuous compliance'.

Quote (A): Notifying authorities may notify only conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 31.
Quote (B): Notifying authorities may notify only conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 31.
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Approval decision on who may act as checker; standard = Art. 31 requirements.
Note (B): Approval decision on who may act as notified body; standard = Art. 31 requirements.

Quote (A): Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission, of each conformity assessment body referred to in paragraph 1.
Quote (B): Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission, of each conformity assessment body referred to in paragraph 1.
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Notification includes activities, modules, AI types and attestation of competence; without accreditation, documentary evidence and monitoring arrangements (30(3)). Also coded Coordination/Resources.
Note (B): Notification link to the Commission and other Member States, with full details of activities, modules, types of AI systems and attestation of competence (30(3)). Also coded Coordination/Resources (the tool).

Quote (A): using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission
Quote (B): the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Shared tool for notifications (also used for changes, Art. 36(1)).
Note (B): Tool serving notification of notified bodies (previous entry).

Quote (A): The conformity assessment body concerned may perform the activities of a notified body only where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States within two weeks of a notification
Quote (B): The conformity assessment body concerned may perform the activities of a notified body only where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States within two weeks of a notification
Holder (A): the Commission or the other Member States
Holder (B): the Commission or the other Member States (may object); the Commission (decides)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution; member-state governments
Note (A): Two weeks with accreditation certificate; two months with documentary evidence. If objections: Commission consults and 'shall decide whether the authorisation is justified' (30(5)).
Note (B): Two weeks where an accreditation certificate is included; two months where documentary evidence is used. 30(5): where objections are raised the Commission consults Member States and the body and 'shall decide whether the authorisation is justified'.

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall be independent of the provider of a high-risk AI system in relation to which they perform conformity assessment activities.
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall be independent of the provider of a high-risk AI system in relation to which they perform conformity assessment activities.
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies [inference: usually private]
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% for breach of Art. 31, 33(1), (3), (4) or 34; designation may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn (Art. 36(4)).
Note (A): Also independent of other operators with an economic interest and of competitors (31(4)); not involved in design, development, marketing or use, no consultancy (31(5)); impartiality procedures (31(6)); confidentiality (31(7)); proportionate procedures (31(8)). 31(1): established under national law with legal personality. Art. 32: presumption of conformity via harmonised standards.
Note (B): Independence of the checker. Also independent of other operators with an economic interest and of competitors. 31(5): neither the body, its top management nor assessment personnel 'shall be directly involved in the design, development, marketing or use of high-risk AI systems'; no consultancy. 31(6): documented impartiality structure and procedures. 31(7): confidentiality and professional secrecy. 31(1): legal personality under national law; 31(3): structure and reporting lines must 'ensure confidence' in results.

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall take out appropriate liability insurance for their conformity assessment activities
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall take out appropriate liability insurance for their conformity assessment activities, unless liability is assumed by the Member State in which they are established in accordance with national law
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Note (A): Consequence-bearing mechanism for the checker's errors, unless liability is assumed by the Member State or the Member State is itself directly responsible.
Note (B): Liability for the checker's work (consequence route). Exception also where the Member State 'is itself directly responsible for the conformity assessment'.

Quote (A): The notified body shall have permanent availability of sufficient administrative, technical, legal and scientific personnel who possess experience and knowledge relating to the relevant types of AI systems, data and data computing
Quote (B): The notified body shall have permanent availability of sufficient administrative, technical, legal and scientific personnel who possess experience and knowledge relating to the relevant types of AI systems
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Note (A): Also 'sufficient internal competences' to evaluate outsourced tasks; 31(2) organisational, quality management, resources and process requirements plus cybersecurity; 31(10) professional integrity and competence. Serves conformity assessment (Arts 34, 43).
Note (B): Staff and expertise for conformity checks (serves Art. 34(1)), also on 'data and data computing' and Section 2 requirements; 'sufficient internal competences to be able effectively to evaluate the tasks conducted by external parties on their behalf'. 31(2): organisational, quality management, resources and process requirements and 'suitable cybersecurity requirements'. 31(10): 'highest degree of professional integrity and the requisite competence'.

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall participate in coordination activities as referred to in Article 38.
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall participate in coordination activities as referred to in Article 38.
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Note (A): Also take part in, or be represented in, European standardisation organisations, or keep up to date with standards.
Note (B): Participation in the sectoral group of notified bodies (Art. 38). They 'shall also take part directly, or be represented in, European standardisation organisations, or ensure that they are aware and up to date in respect of relevant standards'.

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall take full responsibility for the tasks performed by any subcontractors or subsidiaries.
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall take full responsibility for the tasks performed by any subcontractors or subsidiaries.
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part) covers Art. 33(1), (3), (4).
Note (A): 33(1): ensure subcontractor/subsidiary meets Art. 31 and inform notifying authority; 33(4): keep qualification and work documents for the notifying authority for five years.
Note (B): Responsibility stays with the notified body. 33(1): ensure subcontractor or subsidiary meets Art. 31 and inform the notifying authority. 33(3): subcontracting 'only with the agreement of the provider'; 'Notified bodies shall make a list of their subsidiaries publicly available' (publication). 33(4): qualification and work documents kept for the notifying authority for five years.

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems in accordance with the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43.
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems in accordance with the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43.
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Note (A): The third-party check. 34(2): avoid unnecessary burdens, account for size, sector and complexity, minimise burdens for micro and small enterprises, while respecting rigour and protection.
Note (B): Third-party check. Comparator: Section 2 requirements via Art. 43 / Annex VII procedures. 34(2): avoid unnecessary burdens, especially for micro and small enterprises, but 'respect the degree of rigour and the level of protection required'. Notified bodies are only involved for some systems (see Art. 43).

Quote (A): Notified bodies shall make available and submit upon request all relevant documentation, including the providers’ documentation, to the notifying authority referred to in Article 28
Quote (B): Notified bodies shall make available and submit upon request all relevant documentation, including the providers’ documentation, to the notifying authority referred to in Article 28
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Note (A): Lets the notifying authority conduct assessment, designation, notification and monitoring.
Note (B): Answers to the notifying authority, to allow its 'assessment, designation, notification and monitoring activities'.

Quote (A): The Commission shall make publicly available the list of the bodies notified under this Regulation, including their identification numbers and the activities for which they have been notified.
Quote (B): The Commission shall make publicly available the list of the bodies notified under this Regulation, including their identification numbers and the activities for which they have been notified.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Public register of notified bodies, kept up to date; Commission assigns a single identification number to each (35(1)). Also a publication (Accountability) element.
Note (B): Public register of notified bodies, kept up to date; single identification number per body (35(1)). Also a publication (Accountability) element.

Quote (A): it shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible and, in the case of a planned cessation, at least one year before ceasing its activities
Quote (B): it shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible and, in the case of a planned cessation, at least one year before ceasing its activities
Holder (B): a notified body (ceasing activities); the notifying authority
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
Note (A): Trigger: notified body decides to cease activities. Certificates may stay valid nine months if another notified body confirms in writing it assumes responsibility and completes a full assessment; notifying authority withdraws the designation.
Note (B): Notification links on changes. 36(1): notifying authority notifies the Commission and Member States of relevant changes via the electronic tool. 36(3): certificates may stay valid nine months after cessation if another notified body confirms in writing it will assume responsibility and completes a full assessment; notifying authority withdraws the designation. 36(5): a notified body whose designation is suspended, restricted or withdrawn 'shall inform the providers concerned within 10 days'.

Quote (A): require the notified body to suspend or withdraw, within a reasonable period of time determined by the authority, any certificates which were unduly issued
Quote (B): require the notified body to suspend or withdraw, within a reasonable period of time determined by the authority, any certificates which were unduly issued
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Following restriction, suspension or withdrawal of designation. Also: assess impact on certificates (a); inform Commission and Member States of required suspensions (d); inform NCAs of provider's Member State, which take measures to avoid risk to health, safety or fundamental rights (e).
Note (B): Authority over certificates (approvals) already issued, 'in order to ensure the continuing conformity of high-risk AI systems on the market'; Commission and Member States informed (36(7)(d)).

Quote (A): submit a report on its findings to the Commission and the other Member States within three months of having notified the changes to the designation
Quote (B): submit a report on its findings to the Commission and the other Member States within three months of having notified the changes to the designation
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority
Note (A): Notifying authority reports to Commission and Member States; consequence not stated.
Note (B): After restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a designation the notifying authority must (a) assess the impact on certificates and report; (e) give the national competent authorities where the provider is based all relevant information, and 'that authority shall take the appropriate measures, where necessary, to avoid a potential risk to health, safety or fundamental rights'. 36(6): keep the body's files available to other notifying authorities and MSAs.

Quote (A): The Commission shall, where necessary, investigate all cases where there are reasons to doubt the competence of a notified body or the continued fulfilment by a notified body of the requirements laid down in Article 31
Quote (B): The Commission shall, where necessary, investigate all cases where there are reasons to doubt the competence of a notified body or the continued fulfilment by a notified body of the requirements laid down in Article 31
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Commission oversight of notified bodies; notifying authority provides information on request (37(2)); confidentiality (37(3)). Consequence: Art. 37(4).
Note (B): EU-level oversight of notified bodies (and, indirectly, of notifying Member States). Notifying authority must provide information on request (37(2)); confidentiality per Art. 78 (37(3)). Also coded Decision-making/Design (37(4)).

Quote (A): Where the Member State fails to take the necessary corrective measures, the Commission may, by means of an implementing act, suspend, restrict or withdraw the designation.
Quote (B): Where the Member State fails to take the necessary corrective measures, the Commission may, by means of an implementing act, suspend, restrict or withdraw the designation.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): First the Commission requests the notifying Member State to take corrective measures, incl. suspension or withdrawal. Implementing act via examination procedure (Art. 98(2)).
Note (B): Step-in power. First the Commission informs the notifying Member State and requests corrective measures 'including the suspension or withdrawal of the notification if necessary'.

Quote (A): appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies active in the conformity assessment procedures pursuant to this Regulation are put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group of notified bodies
Quote (B): appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies active in the conformity assessment procedures pursuant to this Regulation are put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group of notified bodies
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Commission 'shall ensure'. 38(2): each notifying authority ensures its bodies participate, directly or through representatives.
Note (B): Cross-body group. 'The Commission shall ensure' this. 38(2): each notifying authority 'shall ensure that the bodies notified by it participate'. 38(3): 'The Commission shall provide for the exchange of knowledge and best practices between notifying authorities.'

Quote (A): Conformity assessment bodies established under the law of a third country with which the Union has concluded an agreement may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies under this Regulation
Quote (B): Conformity assessment bodies established under the law of a third country with which the Union has concluded an agreement may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies under this Regulation
Position (A): public authority (authorising body not named)
Note (A): Passive; authorising body not named. Condition: meet Art. 31 or ensure an equivalent level of compliance.
Note (B): Condition: 'provided that they meet the requirements laid down in Article 31 or they ensure an equivalent level of compliance'. Who authorises is not stated.

Quote (A): the Commission shall issue, without undue delay, standardisation requests covering all requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter
Quote (B): the Commission shall issue, without undue delay, standardisation requests covering all requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Also GPAI obligations and deliverables on energy and resource efficiency. Commission must specify standards be clear, consistent and aim to ensure requirements are met, and ask ESOs to evidence best efforts. Also coded Coordination/Design.
Note (B): Sets direction for standards, incl. GPAI obligations and 'deliverables on reporting and documentation processes to improve AI systems’ resource performance' and energy efficiency. Standards must be 'clear, consistent' and aim to ensure systems meet the requirements; Commission requests European standardisation organisations to 'provide evidence of their best efforts'. Also coded Coordination/Design (consultation).

Quote (A): When preparing a standardisation request, the Commission shall consult the Board and relevant stakeholders, including the advisory forum.
Quote (B): When preparing a standardisation request, the Commission shall consult the Board and relevant stakeholders, including the advisory forum.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Consultation step in standard-setting.
Note (B): Consultation link with the Board (Member State representatives) and stakeholders including the advisory forum (Art. 67, outside this part).

Quote (A): to enhance multi-stakeholder governance ensuring a balanced representation of interests and the effective participation of all relevant stakeholders
Quote (B): to enhance multi-stakeholder governance ensuring a balanced representation of interests and the effective participation of all relevant stakeholders
Holder (A): The participants in the standardisation process
Holder (B): The participants in the standardisation process
Position (A): outside the state: standards bodies and participants (mixed)
Note (A): Participants shall also seek to promote investment and innovation, legal certainty, competitiveness, global cooperation, and take into account international standards consistent with Union values and fundamental rights.
Note (B): How standards are to be set. Participants also 'shall seek to promote investment and innovation in AI', legal certainty, competitiveness, global cooperation, and take account of international standards 'consistent with Union values, fundamental rights and interests'.

Quote (A): The Commission may adopt, implementing acts establishing common specifications for the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter
Quote (B): The Commission may adopt, implementing acts establishing common specifications for the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Conditions: standardisation request not accepted, not delivered on time, standards 'insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns', or non-compliant; and no reference published or expected. Conformity with common specifications gives presumption (41(3)); repealed when a harmonised standard is published (41(4)). Also coded Coordination/Design.
Note (B): Fallback standard-setting where standardisation requests are not accepted or delivered on time, where 'the relevant harmonised standards insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns', or do not comply with the request, and no reference is expected soon. Commission 'shall consult the advisory forum'; must inform the Regulation 1025/2012 committee first (41(2)). Conformity with common specifications gives presumption of conformity (41(3)); repealed once harmonised standards are published (41(4)).

Quote (A): it shall inform the Commission thereof with a detailed explanation. The Commission shall assess that information and, if appropriate, amend the implementing act establishing the common specification concerned.
Quote (B): it shall inform the Commission thereof with a detailed explanation. The Commission shall assess that information and, if appropriate, amend the implementing act establishing the common specification concerned.
Holder (A): a Member State (informs); the Commission (assesses, may amend)
Position (A): public authority: member-state government; EU institution
Note (A): Trigger: Member State considers a common specification does not entirely meet the requirements.
Note (B): Feedback route from Member States to the Commission where 'a common specification does not entirely meet the requirements'.

Quote (A): the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9), as applicable, shall act as a notified body
Quote (B): by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9), as applicable, shall act as a notified body
Holder (A): the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9)
Holder (B): the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9)
Position (A): public authority: member-state MSA or EDPS [inference from Art. 3(48)]
Note (A): Applies 'where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies' (Annex III point 1 biometrics). A public checker replaces the notified body for these public-sector deployments.
Note (B): Public-sector-specific: where a biometric high-risk system 'is intended to be put into service by' these public bodies and the notified-body procedure applies, the check is done by the MSA rather than a private notified body. Otherwise 'the provider may choose any of the notified bodies'. [inference] Art. 74(8)-(9) (outside this part) name the relevant MSAs.

Quote (A): providers shall follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control as referred to in Annex VI, which does not provide for the involvement of a notified body
Quote (B): providers shall follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control as referred to in Annex VI, which does not provide for the involvement of a notified body
Holder (B): providers (of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III)
Position (A): mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part); national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
Note (A): For Annex III points 2 to 8. Self-assessment, no third-party check. [inference] Covers most public-sector Annex III uses (essential public services and benefits, law enforcement, migration, justice). Trigger: before placing on market/putting into service (Art. 16(f)); compares against Section 2; metric not stated.
Note (B): Self-assessment by the provider for Annex III points 2-8. [inference] Most public-sector use cases in Annex III (e.g. public services and benefits, law enforcement, migration, justice) are therefore checked by the provider itself, with no third party. 43(3): Annex I Section A products follow the sectoral procedure with Section 2 requirements included; manufacturers may opt out of third-party assessment only if harmonised standards or common specifications cover all Section 2 requirements. Commission may extend Annex VII to these systems (43(6)).

Quote (A): in order to subject high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III to the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Annex VII or parts thereof
Quote (B): in order to subject high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III to the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Annex VII or parts thereof
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Could move public-sector Annex III systems from self-assessment to notified-body assessment, considering effectiveness of internal control and notified-body capacity. 43(5): power to amend Annexes VI and VII.
Note (B): Authority to move Annex III points 2-8 systems from self-assessment to notified-body assessment by delegated act, 'taking into account the effectiveness of the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control ... as well as the availability of adequate capacities and resources among notified bodies'. 43(5): may update Annexes VI and VII.

Quote (A): Where a notified body finds that an AI system no longer meets the requirements set out in Section 2, it shall, taking account of the principle of proportionality, suspend or withdraw the certificate issued or impose restrictions on it
Quote (B): Where a notified body finds that an AI system no longer meets the requirements set out in Section 2, it shall, taking account of the principle of proportionality, suspend or withdraw the certificate issued or impose restrictions on it
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
Note (A): Unless the provider takes corrective action within a deadline set by the notified body; reasons must be given.
Note (B): Authority to suspend or withdraw approval, 'unless compliance with those requirements is ensured by appropriate corrective action taken by the provider of the system within an appropriate deadline set by the notified body'. 'The notified body shall give reasons for its decision.' Also coded Accountability/Design (appeal).

Quote (A): An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
Quote (B): An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
Position (A): not stated (who provides the appeal is not named)
Note (A): Challenge route against notified-body decisions; who runs it, who may appeal, and consequence: not stated.
Note (B): Challenge route against notified-body decisions. Who provides or hears the appeal, and who may appeal, are not stated; nearest named actor: notified bodies.

Quote (A): Each notified body shall provide the other notified bodies carrying out similar conformity assessment activities covering the same types of AI systems with relevant information on issues relating to negative and, on request, positive conformity assessment results.
Quote (B): Each notified body shall provide the other notified bodies carrying out similar conformity assessment activities covering the same types of AI systems with relevant information on issues relating to negative and, on request, positive conformity assessment results.
Position (A): outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
Note (A): 45(2): inform other notified bodies of refused, suspended or withdrawn approvals and certificates. 45(4): confidentiality.
Note (B): Information sharing between checkers. 45(2): inform other notified bodies of refused, suspended or withdrawn QMS approvals and technical documentation certificates (and, on request, issued ones). 45(4): confidentiality per Art. 78.

Quote (A): any market surveillance authority may authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems within the territory of the Member State concerned, for exceptional reasons of public security
Quote (B): any market surveillance authority may authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems within the territory of the Member State concerned
Position (A): public authority: member-state market surveillance authority
Note (A): Also for protection of life and health, environment, key industrial and infrastructural assets. Limited period while conformity assessment proceeds. Only if the MSA concludes the system complies with Section 2 (46(3)). Deemed justified if no objection within 15 days (46(4)).
Note (B): Exemption from Art. 43 'upon a duly justified request', 'for exceptional reasons of public security or the protection of life and health of persons, environmental protection or the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets'. Limited period while conformity assessment is carried out 'without undue delay'. 46(3): issued 'only if the market surveillance authority concludes that the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements of Section 2'. Links to Art. 27(3) (FRIA notification exemption).

Quote (A): law-enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation referred to in paragraph 1, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay
Quote (B): law-enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation referred to in paragraph 1, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay
Holder (A): law-enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
Holder (B): law-enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
Position (A): public authority: member-state law enforcement or civil protection
If not met (A): 'If the authorisation referred to in paragraph 1 is refused, the use of the high-risk AI system shall be stopped with immediate effect and all the results and outputs of such use shall be immediately discarded.'
Note (A): Trigger: duly justified urgency for public security, or specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or physical safety.
Note (B): Public-sector urgency exemption. Trigger: 'a duly justified situation of urgency for exceptional reasons of public security or in the case of specific, substantial and imminent threat to the life or physical safety of natural persons'.

Quote (A): The market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2.
Quote (B): The market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2.
Position (A): public authority: member-state market surveillance authority
Note (A): Excludes sensitive operational data of law-enforcement authorities.
Note (B): Notification link; 'This obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data in relation to the activities of law-enforcement authorities.' 46(4): absent objection within 15 calendar days the authorisation is 'deemed justified'.

Quote (A): By drawing up the EU declaration of conformity, the provider shall assume responsibility for compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2.
Quote (B): By drawing up the EU declaration of conformity, the provider shall assume responsibility for compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2.
Position (A): mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
If not met (A): Not stated here. Missing or incorrect EU declaration is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(c)-(d)): MSA requires remedy, then restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws; Art. 16(g) breach fined under Art. 99(4)(a) (both outside this part).
Note (A): Provider sign-off. 47(1): written, machine-readable, physical or e-signed declaration per system, kept 10 years for NCAs, copy on request; 47(2): content per Annex V, translated; 47(3): single declaration across Union law; kept up to date.
Note (B): Sign-off. 47(1): written, machine-readable, physical or electronically signed declaration for each system, kept for national competent authorities 10 years, copy on request. 47(2): states Section 2 requirements met; content Annex V; translated. 47(3): single declaration where other Union legislation applies. Keep up to date. 47(5): Commission may amend Annex V by delegated act.

Quote (A): The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems.
Quote (B): The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems.
Holder (B): not stated (passive); nearest: providers (Art. 16(h)); notified body or provider/authorised representative affixes the notified body number
Position (A): mixed (nearest actor: provider, Art. 16(h))
If not met (A): Not stated here. CE marking not affixed or affixed in violation is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(a)-(b), outside this part); Art. 16(h) breach fined under Art. 99(4)(a).
Note (A): Public sign of conformity. Digital CE marking for digital systems (48(2)); followed by notified body identification number where applicable, incl. in promotional material (48(4)).

Quote (A): pursuant to a specific sandbox plan agreed between the providers or prospective providers and the competent authority

Quote (A): If both the provider or prospective provider and the national competent authority explicitly agree, the exit report may be made publicly available through the single information platform referred to in this Article.

Note (B): Publication is optional and needs both parties' agreement. Art. 57(9) (objectives of sandboxes, begins p. 88) states aims only and is not coded.

Quote (A): the national data protection authorities and those other national or competent authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox and involved in the supervision of those aspects
Quote (B): the national data protection authorities and those other national or competent authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox and involved in the supervision of those aspects

Art. 57(1)-(9) begin before this part's line range and are not coded here.
Note (B): Verb: 'shall ensure'. Trigger: sandboxed AI systems that process personal data or fall under other authorities' remit. Links the sandbox authority with data protection and other supervisors.

Quote (A): National competent authorities shall have the power to temporarily or permanently suspend the testing process, or the participation in the sandbox if no effective mitigation is possible
