Note (A): Authority to pause or stop. Trigger: significant risks to health and safety or fundamental rights identified during development and testing, with no effective mitigation possible. Sandboxes 'shall not affect the supervisory or corrective powers of the competent authorities'. Also coded Coordination/Design (inform AI Office) and Delivery/Design (mitigation).
Note (B): Authority to pause or stop sandbox testing. Trigger: significant risks to health, safety or fundamental rights that cannot be effectively mitigated. Duty to inform the AI Office is coordination (not coded separately). See Delivery/Design entry on mitigation, same paragraph.

Quote (A): Any significant risks to health and safety and fundamental rights identified during the development and testing of such AI systems shall result in an adequate mitigation.
Quote (B): Any significant risks to health and safety and fundamental rights identified during the development and testing of such AI systems shall result in an adequate mitigation.
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): suspension of testing or of sandbox participation where no effective mitigation is possible (Art. 57(11))
Note (A): Passive. Nearest named actors: providers or prospective providers in the sandbox and the supervising national competent authority. Trigger: risk identified during development and testing; compared against: not stated; metric: not stated. Also coded Decision-making/Design.
Note (B): Passive 'shall result in'. Nearest named actors: sandbox participants (prospective providers) and the supervising national competent authorities. Trigger: risks identified during development and testing; comparator and metric not stated. Also coded Decision-making/Design (suspension power).

Quote (A): Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox shall remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage inflicted on third parties
Quote (B): Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox shall remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage inflicted on third parties
Holder (A): Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox
Holder (B): Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (prospective providers may also be public authorities, Art. 59(1)(a))
If not met (A): liability under applicable Union and national liability law for damage inflicted on third parties
Note (A): Answer to: third parties harmed, via liability law; consequence: civil liability. Also coded Accountability/Design (fine exemption).
Note (B): Answer to: injured third parties, through liability law. Shield from fines: 'provided that the prospective providers observe the specific plan and the terms and conditions for their participation and follow in good faith the guidance given by the national competent authority, no administrative fines shall be imposed'. Same applies to other law where other authorities were involved.

Quote (A): National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.
Quote (B): National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Board = European Artificial Intelligence Board (Art. 65).
Note (B): Cross-government network at EU level (the Board). Related: Art. 57(13) sandboxes 'shall be designed and implemented in such a way that, where relevant, they facilitate cross-border cooperation between national competent authorities'.

Quote (A): National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox
Quote (B): National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Notification. Also coded Delivery/Resources (support and guidance on request) and Coordination/Design (public list).
Note (B): Notification. Same paragraph: they 'may ask them for support and guidance' (coded Delivery/Resources).

Quote (A): and may ask them for support and guidance.
Quote (B): and may ask them for support and guidance
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office) and EU body (Board)
Level of obligation (A): n/a (provided on request); statutory power to request
Note (A): Support available to national competent authorities operating sandboxes, in which systems are developed and tested under supervision. Offered by named EU actors on request; no duty on the AI Office or Board to give it is stated.
Note (B): Support available to national competent authorities on request. Serves their duty to establish and run sandboxes (earlier in Art. 57, outside part 3). Could also be read as Coordination.

Quote (A): The AI Office shall make publicly available a list of planned and existing sandboxes and keep it up to date
Quote (B): The AI Office shall make publicly available a list of planned and existing sandboxes and keep it up to date
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office, within the Commission)
Note (A): Purpose stated: 'to encourage more interaction in the AI regulatory sandboxes and cross-border cooperation'. A public register; could also be read as Accountability (publication).
Note (B): Public register. Stated purpose: 'in order to encourage more interaction in the AI regulatory sandboxes and cross-border cooperation', so coded Coordination rather than Accountability.

Quote (A): National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board
Quote (B): National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board, from one year after the establishment of the AI regulatory sandbox and every year thereafter until its termination, and a final report.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Answer to: AI Office and Board; consequence: not stated (the Commission 'shall, where appropriate, take the annual reports into account'). Timing: from one year after establishment, every year until termination, plus a final report. Content: progress and results, best practices, incidents, lessons learnt, recommendations on setup and on application or revision of the Regulation. Also coded Accountability/Design (publication).
Note (B): Answer to: AI Office and Board. Content: progress, results, best practices, incidents, lessons learnt, recommendations. Consequence: the Commission 'shall, where appropriate, take the annual reports into account'. Publication coded separately.

Quote (A): The national competent authorities shall make those annual reports or abstracts thereof available to the public, online.
Quote (B): The national competent authorities shall make those annual reports or abstracts thereof available to the public, online.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Publication to the public. Abstracts are allowed instead of full reports.
Note (B): Publication to the public; abstracts are enough. Also coded Accountability/Design (reporting), same paragraph.

Quote (A): The Commission shall develop a single and dedicated interface containing all relevant information related to AI regulatory sandboxes to allow stakeholders to interact with AI regulatory sandboxes and to raise enquiries with competent authorities
Quote (B): The Commission shall develop a single and dedicated interface containing all relevant information related to AI regulatory sandboxes to allow stakeholders to interact with AI regulatory sandboxes and to raise enquiries with competent authorities
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Tool provided by a named actor. Also lets stakeholders 'seek non-binding guidance on the conformity of innovative products, services, business models embedding AI technologies' (Art. 62(1)(c)). Also coded Coordination/Design (proactive coordination).
Note (B): Tool that connects stakeholders with authorities. Also lets them 'seek non-binding guidance on the conformity of innovative products, services, business models embedding AI technologies'. The Commission 'shall proactively coordinate with national competent authorities, where relevant'.

Quote (A): the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of the AI regulatory sandboxes.
Quote (B): the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of the AI regulatory sandboxes
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Standard-setting. Common principles on: eligibility and selection criteria; procedures for application, participation, monitoring, exiting and termination, including the sandbox plan and exit report; terms and conditions for participants. Adopted by examination procedure (Art. 98(2)), i.e. with a committee of Member States.
Note (B): Standard-setting. Common principles on eligibility and selection criteria; procedures for application, monitoring, exit and termination (incl. sandbox plan and exit report); terms and conditions. Adopted by the examination procedure in Art. 98(2) (member-state committee).

Quote (A): national competent authorities inform applicants of their decision within three months of the application
Quote (B): national competent authorities inform applicants of their decision within three months of the application
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty (content the implementing acts 'shall ensure')
Note (A): Admission decision. Sandboxes are open to any applying provider or prospective provider who meets eligibility and selection criteria 'which shall be transparent and fair'.
Note (B): NCAs decide who enters a sandbox. Criteria 'shall be transparent and fair'. Art. 58(2)(h): participation period 'may be extended by the national competent authority'. Art. 58(2)(b): providers 'may also submit applications in partnerships with deployers'.

Quote (A): access to the AI regulatory sandboxes is free of charge for SMEs, including start-ups, without prejudice to exceptional costs that national competent authorities may recover in a fair and proportionate manner
Quote (B): access to the AI regulatory sandboxes is free of charge for SMEs, including start-ups
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Free access serves supervised development and testing in sandboxes (Art. 57). Holder inferred from the cost-recovery clause.
Note (B): Nearest named actor: national competent authorities, which 'may recover' exceptional costs 'in a fair and proportionate manner'. Serves providers' compliance work in sandboxes.

Quote (A): AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate the development of tools and infrastructure for testing, benchmarking, assessing and explaining dimensions of AI systems relevant for regulatory learning, such as accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
Quote (B): AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate the development of tools and infrastructure for testing, benchmarking, assessing and explaining dimensions of AI systems relevant for regulatory learning, such as accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Testing and benchmarking tools; also 'measures to mitigate risks to fundamental rights and society at large'. Serves testing and evaluation. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities; Commission via implementing acts.
Note (B): Testing tools and infrastructure; also 'measures to mitigate risks to fundamental rights and society at large'. Nearest actor: national competent authorities running sandboxes. Serves testing and evaluation.

Quote (A): Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandboxes, in particular SMEs and start-ups, shall be directed, where relevant, to pre-deployment services such as guidance on the implementation of this Regulation
Quote (B): Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandboxes, in particular SMEs and start-ups, shall be directed, where relevant, to pre-deployment services such as guidance on the implementation of this Regulation
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Points to services: guidance, help with standardisation documents and certification, testing and experimentation facilities, European Digital Innovation Hubs, centres of excellence. Providers of these services not named; a referral, not an offer by a named actor. Nearest named actor: national competent authorities.
Note (B): Passive. Nearest actor: sandbox authorities. Services named: guidance, help with standardisation documents and certification, testing and experimentation facilities, European Digital Innovation Hubs, centres of excellence. Who offers them is not named; a pointer, not a stated offer.

Quote (A): they shall specifically agree the terms and conditions of such testing and, in particular, the appropriate safeguards with the participants, with a view to protecting fundamental rights, health and safety
Quote (B): they shall specifically agree the terms and conditions of such testing and, in particular, the appropriate safeguards with the participants, with a view to protecting fundamental rights, health and safety
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Trigger: national competent authorities consider authorising testing in real world conditions within a sandbox. Also coded Coordination/Design (cooperation with other authorities).
Note (B): Trigger: NCAs consider authorising real-world testing inside a sandbox. Also 'they shall cooperate with other national competent authorities with a view to ensuring consistent practices' (coordination, not coded separately).

Quote (A): there are effective monitoring mechanisms to identify if any high risks to the rights and freedoms of the data subjects
Quote (B): effective monitoring mechanisms to identify if any high risks to the rights and freedoms of the data subjects
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Note (A): Monitoring check. Trigger: ongoing during sandbox experimentation. Compared against: high risks as referred to in Art. 35 GDPR and Art. 39 Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. Metric: not stated. Also requires 'response mechanisms to promptly mitigate those risks and, where necessary, stop the processing'. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.
Note (B): Nearest actor: prospective provider (data under its control, point (d)). Trigger: ongoing during sandbox experimentation. Comparator: high risks under GDPR Art. 35 / EUDPR Art. 39. Also requires 'response mechanisms to promptly mitigate those risks and, where necessary, stop the processing'.

Quote (A): any processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox neither leads to measures or decisions affecting the data subjects
Quote (B): any processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox neither leads to measures or decisions affecting the data subjects
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Note (A): Limits use: sandbox processing must not feed decisions about the data subjects, nor affect their data protection rights. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.
Note (B): Limit: sandbox processing may not be used for decisions about data subjects. Nearest actor: prospective provider.

Quote (A): a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the training, testing and validation of the AI system is kept together with the testing results as part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV
Quote (B): a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the training, testing and validation of the AI system is kept together with the testing results
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Note (A): Recording of training, testing and validation with results. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.
Note (B): Record-keeping, kept 'as part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV'. Point (h): processing logs kept for the duration of participation. Nearest actor: prospective provider.

Quote (A): a short summary of the AI project developed in the sandbox, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities
Quote (B): a short summary of the AI project developed in the sandbox, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority (competent authorities' website)
If not met (A): [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Note (A): Publication. Exception: 'this obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data in relation to the activities of law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities'. Passive; nearest named actor: the competent authorities.
Note (B): Publication to the public. Who publishes is not stated; nearest named actor: the competent authorities (their website). Public-sector exemption: 'this obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data in relation to the activities of law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities'.

Quote (A): The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, specify the detailed elements of the real-world testing plan.
Quote (B): The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, specify the detailed elements of the real-world testing plan.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Standard for testing plans; examination procedure (Art. 98(2)).
Note (B): Standard-setting for real-world testing of Annex III high-risk systems outside sandboxes. Examination procedure Art. 98(2).

Quote (A): the market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted has approved the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan
Quote (B): the market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted has approved the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan
Holder (A): Market surveillance authority in the Member State where testing is to be conducted
Holder (B): Market surveillance authority in the Member State where testing is conducted
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Level of obligation (A): mandatory approval gate (statutory), with tacit approval
If not met (A): testing may not be conducted ('only where all of the following conditions are met')
Note (A): Tacit approval: 'where the market surveillance authority has not provided an answer within 30 days' the testing and plan 'shall be understood to have been approved'; where national law has no tacit approval, an authorisation is still required.
Note (B): Trigger: before real-world testing. Point (a): provider draws up the plan and submits it to the MSA. Tacit approval: 'where the market surveillance authority has not provided an answer within 30 days ... shall be understood to have been approved', unless national law requires authorisation. Art. 60(2): providers may test 'in partnership with one or more deployers'.

Quote (A): has registered the testing in real world conditions in accordance with Article 71(4) with a Union-wide unique single identification number and with the information specified in Annex IX
Quote (B): has registered the testing in real world conditions in accordance with Article 71(4) with a Union-wide unique single identification number and with the information specified in Annex IX
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Registration. For law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control (Annex III points 1, 6, 7): registered 'in the secure non-public section of the EU database'; for critical infrastructure (point 2): per Art. 49(5). Testing registrations are visible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission unless the provider consents (Art. 71(4)).
Note (B): Registration in the EU database. Visibility: Art. 71(4) makes Art. 60 registrations accessible only to MSAs and the Commission unless the provider consents. Law-enforcement/migration variant coded separately.

Quote (A): the provider or prospective provider and the deployer or prospective deployer shall conclude an agreement specifying their roles and responsibilities
Quote (B): the provider or prospective provider and the deployer or prospective deployer shall conclude an agreement specifying their roles and responsibilities
Holder (A): Provider or prospective provider; deployer or prospective deployer
Holder (B): Provider or prospective provider and deployer or prospective deployer
Position (A): outside the state: private companies; deployers may be public bodies
Note (A): Supplier-deployer agreement 'with a view to ensuring compliance with the provisions for testing in real world conditions'. [inference] Where the deployer is a public body this is a contractual link with its supplier. Also coded Decision-making/Resources (information to deployers).
Note (B): Supplier-deployer agreement 'with a view to ensuring compliance with the provisions for testing in real world conditions'. Trigger: testing organised with deployers. Also coded Decision-making/Resources (information to deployers), same point.

Quote (A): the latter have been informed of all aspects of the testing that are relevant to their decision to participate, and given the relevant instructions for use of the AI system referred to in Article 13
Quote (B): the latter have been informed of all aspects of the testing that are relevant to their decision to participate, and given the relevant instructions for use of the AI system
Holder (A): Provider or prospective provider (provides to deployers)
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
Level of obligation (A): statutory condition for testing (required of the provider)
Note (A): Information and instructions for deployers or prospective deployers; serves the deployer's decision to take part. Also coded Coordination/Design.
Note (B): Information for deployers' decision whether to take part. Passive; nearest actor: provider or prospective provider organising the testing. Instructions for use per Art. 13 also serve deployers' use. Also coded Coordination/Design.

Quote (A): the testing in real world conditions is effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider, as well as by deployers or prospective deployers
Quote (B): the testing in real world conditions is effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider, as well as by deployers or prospective deployers
Holder (A): Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
Holder (B): Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
Position (A): outside the state: private companies; deployers may be public bodies
Note (A): Human oversight during testing. Trigger: throughout testing. Also coded Delivery/Resources (qualified persons).
Note (B): Human oversight during testing. Trigger: throughout testing; metric not stated. Also coded Delivery/Resources (qualified persons).

Quote (A): through persons who are suitably qualified in the relevant field and have the necessary capacity, training and authority to perform their tasks
Quote (B): through persons who are suitably qualified in the relevant field and have the necessary capacity, training and authority to perform their tasks
Holder (A): Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
Holder (B): Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
Position (A): outside the state: private companies; deployers may be public bodies
Level of obligation (A): statutory condition for testing (required of the holder)
Note (A): Staff, training and authority required of the holders; serves oversight of testing (Delivery/Design, same point).
Note (B): Staff, training and authority for oversight of testing; required of the holder. Serves the Delivery/Design oversight entry, same point.

Quote (A): the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded.
Quote (B): the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Override of outputs must be possible. Nearest named actors: the provider and the deployers who oversee the testing (Art. 60(4)(j)). Linked to Art. 61(1)(d) (arrangements for requesting reversal).
Note (B): Override of outputs during testing. Who reverses is not stated; nearest actors: provider and deployer overseeing the testing (point (j)).

Quote (A): Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information, of carrying out unannounced remote or on-site inspections
Quote (B): Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information, of carrying out unannounced remote or on-site inspections
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty (Member States) creating statutory powers (market surveillance authorities)
Note (A): Inspection and information powers, plus 'performing checks on the conduct of the testing'. Providers answer to the market surveillance authority. Authorities 'shall use those powers to ensure the safe development of testing'.
Note (B): Inspection powers over real-world testing; also 'performing checks on the conduct of the testing'. Providers answer to the MSA. MSAs 'shall use those powers to ensure the safe development of testing'.

Quote (A): Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73.
Quote (B): Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73.
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Incident reporting to the regulator. Passive; nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Delivery/Design (same paragraph).
Note (B): Passive. Nearest actor: provider or prospective provider (named in the next sentence). Answer to: national MSA. Trigger: serious incident during testing.

Quote (A): The provider or prospective provider shall adopt immediate mitigation measures or, failing that, shall suspend the testing in real world conditions until such mitigation takes place, or otherwise terminate it.
Quote (B): The provider or prospective provider shall adopt immediate mitigation measures or, failing that, shall suspend the testing in real world conditions until such mitigation takes place, or otherwise terminate it.
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Duty to pause or stop. Trigger: serious incident during testing.
Note (B): Duty to pause or stop testing after a serious incident. Also: 'shall establish a procedure for the prompt recall of the AI system upon such termination' (delivery, not coded separately).

Quote (A): Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority
Quote (B): Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted of the suspension or termination
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Notify the authority in the Member State where testing is conducted 'of the suspension or termination of the testing in real world conditions and of the final outcomes'.
Note (B): Reporting to the regulator, also 'of the final outcomes'. Answer to: national MSA.

Quote (A): The provider or prospective provider shall be liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of their testing in real world conditions.
Quote (B): The provider or prospective provider shall be liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of their testing in real world conditions.
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
If not met (A): liability under applicable Union and national liability law
Note (A): Answer to: persons harmed, via liability law.
Note (B): Answer to: persons harmed, through liability law.

Quote (A): the arrangements for requesting the reversal or the disregarding of the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system
Quote (B): the arrangements for requesting the reversal or the disregarding of the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty (information to be given before consent)
Note (A): A route for subjects to challenge outputs during testing; the arrangements themselves are not specified. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Linked to Decision-making/Design (Art. 60(4)(k)).
Note (B): Subjects must be told how to challenge outputs. Nearest actor: provider or its legal representative (point (e) contact details). Answer to: test subjects; consequence not stated.

Quote (A): The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
Quote (B): The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Recording. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider.
Note (B): Recording. Nearest actor: provider or prospective provider.

Quote (A): provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes
Quote (B): provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes

Note (A): Access resource for supervised development and testing; subject to eligibility and selection criteria; does not preclude other SMEs.
Note (B): Priority sandbox access, subject to eligibility and selection criteria. Serves providers' compliance work.

Quote (A): organise specific awareness raising and training activities on the application of this Regulation tailored to the needs of SMEs including start-ups, deployers and, as appropriate, local public authorities
Quote (B): organise specific awareness raising and training activities on the application of this Regulation tailored to the needs of SMEs including start-ups, deployers and, as appropriate, local public authorities
Position (A): public authority: Member State

Note (A): Training provided by a named actor to deployers and local public authorities. Serves compliance with the Regulation generally [inference: including deployer obligations].
Note (B): Training for deployers and local public authorities. Serves their compliance with the Regulation generally.

Quote (A): The specific interests and needs of the SME providers, including start-ups, shall be taken into account when setting the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43, reducing those fees proportionately to their size
Quote (B): The specific interests and needs of the SME providers, including start-ups, shall be taken into account when setting the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Reduced fees serve conformity assessment. Passive; whoever sets the fees is not named (nearest: notified bodies or Member States [inference]).
Note (B): Fee reduction 'proportionately to their size, market size and other relevant indicators'. Who sets fees is not stated. Serves conformity assessment.

Quote (A): provide standardised templates for areas covered by this Regulation, as specified by the Board in its request
Quote (B): provide standardised templates for areas covered by this Regulation, as specified by the Board in its request

Note (A): Templates; content set by the Board's request.
Note (B): Templates. The Board specifies which areas. Serves compliance generally.

Quote (A): develop and maintain a single information platform providing easy to use information in relation to this Regulation for all operators across the Union
Quote (B): develop and maintain a single information platform providing easy to use information in relation to this Regulation for all operators across the Union

Note (A): Information resource for all operators, including public-sector deployers [inference].
Note (B): Information resource for all operators (incl. public deployers). Also (c): 'organise appropriate communication campaigns to raise awareness about the obligations arising from this Regulation'.

Quote (A): evaluate and promote the convergence of best practices in public procurement procedures in relation to AI systems.

Quote (A): Microenterprises within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 of this Regulation in a simplified manner

Note (B): Scope/exemption. Limit, Art. 63(2): not 'exempting those operators from fulfilling any other requirements or obligations laid down in this Regulation, including those established in Articles 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 72 and 73'.

Quote (A): the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system which may be complied with in a simplified manner considering the needs of microenterprises
Quote (B): the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system which may be complied with in a simplified manner

Note (B): Guidance for microenterprises, 'without affecting the level of protection'. Serves the quality management system duty (Art. 17, outside part 3).

Quote (A): The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office.
Quote (B): The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office.

Note (A): Capacity for the AI Office's supervisory and enforcement tasks (e.g. Arts. 75, 88-94). Function assignment is coder judgement; it also serves Decision-making.
Note (B): General capacity for the AI Office's tasks, incl. supervision of general-purpose AI models (Arts 88-94). Function assignment is a judgement; the capacity also serves coordination and support. Art. 64(2): 'Member States shall facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office'.

Quote (A): The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State. The European Data Protection Supervisor shall participate as observer.
Quote (B): The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State. The European Data Protection Supervisor shall participate as observer.

Note (A): Cross-government group established by Art. 65(1). AI Office attends without voting; other national and Union authorities, bodies or experts may be invited case by case. Representatives designated for three years, renewable once (Art. 65(3)).
Note (B): Cross-government body. The AI Office attends 'without taking part in the votes'; others may be invited case by case. Representatives designated for three years, renewable once (65(3)); rules of procedure by two-thirds majority (65(5)).

Quote (A): are designated as a single contact point vis-à-vis the Board and, where appropriate, taking into account Member States’ needs, as a single contact point for stakeholders
Quote (B): are designated as a single contact point vis-à-vis the Board and, where appropriate, taking into account Member States’ needs, as a single contact point for stakeholders
Position (A): public authority: Member State
Note (A): Contact point. Verb: Member States 'shall ensure'.
Note (B): Contact point. Also (c): representatives 'empowered to facilitate consistency and coordination between national competent authorities in their Member State'.

Quote (A): The Board shall establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities
Quote (B): The Board shall establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities
Position (A): public authority: EU body (Member State representatives)
Note (A): The market surveillance sub-group 'should act as the administrative cooperation group (ADCO)' under Art. 30 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. The Board may set up other sub-groups; advisory forum representatives may be invited as observers. Art. 65(7): Board to safeguard objectivity and impartiality.
Note (B): The market surveillance sub-group 'should act as the administrative cooperation group (ADCO)'. The Board may set up other sub-groups and invite advisory forum representatives as observers.

Quote (A): The AI Office shall provide the secretariat for the Board, convene the meetings upon request of the Chair, and prepare the agenda
Quote (B): The AI Office shall provide the secretariat for the Board, convene the meetings upon request of the Chair, and prepare the agenda
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office, within the Commission)
Note (A): Secretariat support for the Board.
Note (B): Secretariat support for the Board. The Board is chaired by a member-state representative.

Quote (A): support the Commission in promoting AI literacy, public awareness and understanding of the benefits, risks, safeguards and rights and obligations in relation to the use of AI systems
Quote (B): support the Commission in promoting AI literacy, public awareness and understanding of the benefits, risks, safeguards and rights and obligations in relation to the use of AI systems
Position (A): public authority: EU body (Member State representatives)
Note (A): AI literacy resource [inference: supports the AI literacy duty of providers and deployers set out earlier in the Act].
Note (B): Skills and awareness. Serves users of AI systems generally [inference: including public officials].

Quote (A): assist national competent authorities and the Commission in developing the organisational and technical expertise required for the implementation of this Regulation, including by contributing to the assessment of training needs for staff of Member States
Quote (B): assist national competent authorities and the Commission in developing the organisational and technical expertise required for the implementation of this Regulation, including by contributing to the assessment of training needs for staff of Member States

Note (B): Expertise and training for supervisors. Serves NCAs' and the Commission's supervision and enforcement [judgement on function]. Also (k): assist the AI Office in supporting NCAs to set up sandboxes.

Quote (A): The advisory forum shall prepare an annual report on its activities. That report shall be made publicly available.
Quote (B): The advisory forum shall prepare an annual report on its activities. That report shall be made publicly available.
Position (A): mixed (see Art. 67(1) entry)
Note (A): Publication. Answer to: the public; consequence not stated.
Note (B): Publication. Answer to: the public; consequence not stated.

Quote (A): providing advice on the classification of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
Quote (B): providing advice on the classification of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

Note (A): Advice serving the Commission's classification decisions; also advice on classification of various general-purpose models and systems (iv).
Note (B): Advice serving the classification decision on systemic-risk models (decision under Art. 52, outside part 3). Also (iv): advice on classification of various general-purpose AI models and systems.

Quote (A): Each expert shall draw up a declaration of interests, which shall be made publicly available.
Quote (B): Each expert shall draw up a declaration of interests, which shall be made publicly available.
Holder (A): Experts on the scientific panel; AI Office
Holder (B): Each expert on the scientific panel; AI Office
Position (A): outside the state: independent experts; AI Office is public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Publication of interests. Experts must act with impartiality and objectivity, keep information confidential and 'neither seek nor take instructions from anyone'. The AI Office 'shall establish systems and procedures to actively manage and prevent potential conflicts of interest'.
Note (B): Publication of interests. Experts 'shall neither seek nor take instructions from anyone'. The AI Office 'shall establish systems and procedures to actively manage and prevent potential conflicts of interest'.

Quote (A): Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities under this Regulation.
Quote (B): Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities under this Regulation.
Holder (A): Member States (may call on experts); Commission (facilitates access)
Position (A): public authority: Member State; public authority: EU institution
Level of obligation (A): statutory power ('may'); n/a (provided, possibly for a fee)
Note (A): Outside expertise for enforcement. 'The Member States may be required to pay fees'; structure set in the Art. 68(1) implementing act. The Commission 'shall facilitate timely access' and coordinate with Union AI testing support (Art. 84).
Note (B): Expert support for national enforcement. Art. 69(2): Member States 'may be required to pay fees'. Art. 69(3): the Commission 'shall facilitate timely access to the experts'.

Quote (A): Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation.

Note (A): Appointing who decides. Authorities 'shall exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias'; tasks may be split across several authorities.
Note (B): Appoints who supervises and enforces. These authorities 'shall exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias'.

Quote (A): Member States shall designate a market surveillance authority to act as the single point of contact for this Regulation
Quote (B): Member States shall designate a market surveillance authority to act as the single point of contact for this Regulation
Position (A): public authority: Member State; public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Contact point. Member States also communicate the identity and tasks of their authorities to the Commission and 'make publicly available information on how competent authorities and single points of contact can be contacted' by 2 August 2025; 'The Commission shall make a list of the single points of contact publicly available'.
Note (B): Contact point. Member States communicate authorities' identity and tasks to the Commission and publish contact details electronically by 2 August 2025. 'The Commission shall make a list of the single points of contact publicly available.'

Quote (A): Member States shall ensure that their national competent authorities are provided with adequate technical, financial and human resources, and with infrastructure to fulfil their tasks effectively under this Regulation.
Quote (B): Member States shall ensure that their national competent authorities are provided with adequate technical, financial and human resources, and with infrastructure to fulfil their tasks effectively under this Regulation.

Note (A): Money, staff and infrastructure for supervisors. Staff competences must include 'an in-depth understanding of AI technologies, data and data computing, personal data protection, cybersecurity, fundamental rights, health and safety risks and knowledge of existing standards and legal requirements'. Member States assess and update annually. Serves supervision (Accountability) and also Decision-making.
Note (B): Resources for supervisors. Staff competences to include AI, data, data protection, cybersecurity, 'fundamental rights, health and safety risks'. Reviewed annually. Serves NCAs' supervision and enforcement [function a judgement].

Quote (A): By 2 August 2025, and once every two years thereafter, Member States shall report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources of the national competent authorities, with an assessment of their adequacy.
Quote (B): By 2 August 2025, and once every two years thereafter, Member States shall report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources of the national competent authorities, with an assessment of their adequacy.

Note (A): Answer to: the Commission; the Commission transmits the information 'to the Board for discussion and possible recommendations'. No consequence stated.
Note (B): Answer to: the Commission. Consequence: 'The Commission shall transmit that information to the Board for discussion and possible recommendations.'

Quote (A): The Commission shall facilitate the exchange of experience between national competent authorities.
Quote (B): The Commission shall facilitate the exchange of experience between national competent authorities.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (B): Network between national supervisors.

Note (B): Guidance, taking into account Board and Commission guidance. Where other Union law applies, 'the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted' (coordination, not coded separately).

Quote (A): The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database containing information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article concerning high-risk AI systems
Quote (B): The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database containing information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article concerning high-risk AI systems

Note (A): Shared register of high-risk systems (registered under Arts. 49 and 60) and of systems claimed not high-risk under Art. 6(3)-(4). The Commission consults experts on functional specifications and the Board on updates. The Commission is controller (Art. 71(6)).
Note (B): Shared register of Annex III high-risk systems and of systems registered as not high-risk under Art. 6(4). Commission consults experts on functional specifications and 'shall consult the Board' when updating them.

Quote (A): The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or, where applicable, by the authorised representative.
Quote (B): The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or, where applicable, by the authorised representative.

Holder (B): Provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative

Note (A): Registration. Contents coded under Annex VIII Sections A and B.
Note (B): Registration. Public per Art. 71(4) except the non-public section. Content: Annex VIII Sections A and B (coded separately).

Quote (A): The data listed in Section C of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body
Quote (B): The data listed in Section C of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body

Holder (B): Deployer who is, or acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body
Position (A): public authority (or acting on behalf of one)
If not met (A): not stated in this Article; [inference] deployer obligations under Art. 26 attract fines under Art. 99(4)(e), but Art. 99(8) leaves fines on public authorities to each Member State
Note (A): Registration by public-sector deployers, 'in accordance with Article 49(3) and (4)'. Section C includes a summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment findings (coded under Annex VIII). Answer to: the public (Art. 71(4)), except the non-public section under Art. 49(4).
Note (B): Public-sector registration duty, 'in accordance with Article 49(3) and (4)'. Content: Annex VIII Section C, incl. a summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment (coded separately). Published per Art. 71(4) except the Art. 49(4) non-public section.

Quote (A): the information contained in the EU database registered in accordance with Article 49 shall be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly manner.
Quote (B): With the exception of the section referred to in Article 49(4) and Article 60(4), point (c), the information contained in the EU database registered in accordance with Article 49 shall be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly manner.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (Commission as controller, Art. 71(6))
Note (A): Publication. Exceptions: the section under Art. 49(4) [inference: secure non-public section for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control] and Art. 60(4)(c). Testing registrations under Art. 60 are 'accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission' unless the provider consents. 'The information should be easily navigable and machine-readable' (should). Passive; nearest named actor: Commission.
Note (B): Publication. Nearest named actor: the Commission, controller of the database (71(6)). 'should be easily navigable and machine-readable'. Exceptions: the non-public section (law enforcement, migration etc.); Art. 60 testing information 'accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission' unless the provider consents.

Quote (A): That information shall include the names and contact details of natural persons who are responsible for registering the system and have the legal authority to represent the provider or the deployer, as applicable.
Quote (B): That information shall include the names and contact details of natural persons who are responsible for registering the system and have the legal authority to represent the provider or the deployer, as applicable.

Note (A): Named accountable person in the register. Personal data limited to what is necessary.
Note (B): Named responsible persons for registration, for providers and deployers. Personal data limited to what is necessary.

Quote (B): It shall make available to providers, prospective providers and deployers adequate technical and administrative support.

Quote (A): Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system.

Note (B): Monitoring. Trigger: ongoing, throughout the lifetime. Comparator: requirements in Chapter III, Section 2 (72(2)). Microenterprises are not exempt (Art. 63(2)).

Quote (A): The post-market monitoring system shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime
Quote (B): shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data which may be provided by deployers or which may be collected through other sources on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime

Note (B): Purpose: to 'evaluate the continuous compliance' with Chapter III, Section 2; 'where relevant' includes interaction with other AI systems. Public-sector carve-out: 'This obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data of deployers which are law-enforcement authorities.'

Art. 72(4) lets providers under Annex I Section A legislation, and financial institutions for Annex III point 5 systems, integrate into existing systems.
Note (B): Template for the monitoring plan, which is part of Annex IV technical documentation. Also sets content, so partly standard-setting.

Quote (A): Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.
Quote (B): Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.
Holder (A): Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
Holder (B): Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (providers may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Answer to: market surveillance authority. Deadlines: immediately after a causal link is established or reasonably likely, 'not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware'; two days for widespread infringement or Art. 3(49)(b) incidents; ten days in case of death (provider 'or the deployer' establishes or suspects the link); an incomplete initial report is allowed. Art. 73(9)-(10): limited to Art. 3(49)(c) incidents for providers under equivalent Union reporting rules and for medical devices.
Note (B): Answer to: MSA. Timing: immediately after a causal link (or reasonable likelihood) is established and no later than 15 days after awareness (73(2)); 2 days for widespread infringement or point (49)(b) incidents (73(3)); 10 days for a death (73(4)). Deployers' awareness also starts the clock. Initial incomplete report allowed (73(5)). Narrower duty for sectors with equivalent rules (73(9)-(10)).

Quote (A): the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned. This shall include a risk assessment of the incident, and corrective action.
Quote (B): the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned. This shall include a risk assessment of the incident, and corrective action.
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (providers may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Investigation. Trigger: after reporting a serious incident. Also coded Accountability/Design (cooperation and no alteration).
Note (B): Trigger: after reporting a serious incident. Provider 'shall cooperate with the competent authorities' and shall not alter the system in a way that may affect evaluation of causes 'prior to informing the competent authorities'.

Quote (A): Upon receiving a notification related to a serious incident referred to in Article 3, point (49)(c), the relevant market surveillance authority shall inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).
Quote (B): Upon receiving a notification related to a serious incident referred to in Article 3, point (49)(c), the relevant market surveillance authority shall inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).

Note (A): Referral to fundamental-rights bodies. [inference] Point (49)(c) concerns infringement of obligations protecting fundamental rights; the definition sits in Art. 3, outside this part.
Note (B): Referral to fundamental rights bodies. Point (49)(c) is defined in Art. 3 (outside part 3) [not checked here; understood to concern fundamental rights infringements].

Quote (A): The Commission shall develop dedicated guidance to facilitate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.
Quote (B): The Commission shall develop dedicated guidance to facilitate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.

Note (A): Guidance on incident reporting, 'issued by 2 August 2025, and ... assessed regularly'.
Note (B): Guidance on serious incident reporting, due by 2 August 2025 and 'assessed regularly'. Serves the Art. 73(1) reporting duty.

Quote (A): The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days from the date it received the notification
Quote (B): The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days from the date it received the notification referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority

Note (B): Authority to act on a reported serious incident within seven days; measures defined in Regulation 2019/1020 Art. 19 (outside this document). Follows that Regulation's notification procedures.

Quote (A): National competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have taken action on it
Quote (B): National competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident, whether or not they have taken action on it
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): In accordance with Art. 20 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
Note (B): Notification to the EU level, per Regulation 2019/1020 Art. 20.

Quote (A): They shall also annually report to the Commission about the use of prohibited practices that occurred during that year and about the measures taken.
Quote (B): They shall also annually report to the Commission about the use of prohibited practices that occurred during that year and about the measures taken.

Note (B): Answer to: the Commission. Also report annually to the Commission and national competition authorities on information of interest for competition law.

Quote (A): Member States shall designate as market surveillance authorities for the purposes of this Regulation either the competent data protection supervisory authorities under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Directive (EU) 2016/680

Note (B): Appoints supervisors of public-sector high-risk AI: Annex III point 1 used for law enforcement, border management, justice and democracy, and points 6, 7, 8. Quote (A): Member States shall facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under this Regulation and other relevant national authorities or bodies which supervise the application of Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, or in other Union law
Quote (B): Member States shall facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under this Regulation and other relevant national authorities or bodies which supervise the application of Union harmonisation legislation

Note (B): Links AI Act supervisors with sectoral supervisors relevant to Annex III high-risk systems.

Quote (A): Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations
Quote (B): Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations

Quote (B): The AI Office shall provide coordination support for joint investigations.

Quote (B): the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets used for the development of high-risk AI systems

Quote (A): they shall cooperate with the AI Office to carry out compliance evaluations, and shall inform the Board and other market surveillance authorities accordingly.
Quote (B): they shall cooperate with the AI Office to carry out compliance evaluations, and shall inform the Board and other market surveillance authorities accordingly.

Quote (B): it may submit a reasoned request to the AI Office, by which access to that information shall be enforced

Quote (A): to suspend or terminate the testing in real world conditions;

Note (B): Trigger: informed of a serious incident, or grounds to consider Arts 60-61 conditions unmet. Alternative (b): require provider and deployer 'to modify any aspect of the testing'.

Quote (A): the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection.
Quote (B): the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection.

Note (A): Reasons and a challenge route, for providers (not for test subjects).
Note (B): The MSA answers to the provider: reasons and a challenge route for suspension, termination, modification or objection to a testing plan.

Quote (A): it shall communicate the grounds therefor to the market surveillance authorities of other Member States in which the AI system has been tested in accordance with the testing plan.

Quote (A): shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format
Quote (B): shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format

[inference] Covers documentation held by public-sector deployers. Also coded Coordination/Design (inform market surveillance authority).
Note (B): Covers use of Annex III high-risk systems; 'when access to that documentation is necessary for effectively fulfilling their mandates'. The body 'shall inform the market surveillance authority' of any request (coordination). Confidentiality per Art. 78 (77(4)).

Quote (A): By 2 November 2024, each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available.
Quote (B): each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available.

Note (A): Public list; notified to the Commission and other Member States and kept up to date.

Quote (A): The market surveillance authority shall organise the testing with the close involvement of the requesting public authority or body within a reasonable time following the request.
Quote (B): The market surveillance authority shall organise the testing with the close involvement of the requesting public authority or body within a reasonable time following the request.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Technical testing of a high-risk system by a regulator. Trigger: documentation insufficient to ascertain whether fundamental-rights law has been infringed, plus a reasoned request. Compared against: Union law protecting fundamental rights. Metric: not stated. Regulatory check [could also be read as Accountability]. Also coded Coordination/Design (request).
Note (B): Technical testing of a high-risk system. Trigger: fundamental rights body's reasoned request where documentation is 'insufficient to ascertain whether an infringement' occurred. Comparator: Union fundamental rights law; metric not stated.

Quote (A): respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities
Quote (B): shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities

Holder (B): The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and any other natural or legal person involved in applying the Regulation
Position (A): mixed: public authority (Commission, market surveillance authorities) and notified bodies
Note (A): Limits disclosure. Protects intellectual property and trade secrets 'including source code', effective implementation (inspections, investigations, audits), public and national security, criminal or administrative proceedings, classified information. Art. 78(2): authorities request only data 'strictly necessary', protect it and delete it when no longer needed. [inference] Constrains what supervisors can publish about public-sector tools.
Note (B): Limits disclosure rather than creating answerability: protects IP and trade secrets 'including source code', inspections, public and national security, proceedings, classified information. 78(2): request only strictly necessary data; delete when no longer needed. Could also be read as Coordination.

Quote (A): information exchanged on a confidential basis between the national competent authorities or between national competent authorities and the Commission shall not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating national competent authority and the deployer
Quote (B): information exchanged on a confidential basis between the national competent authorities or between national competent authorities and the Commission shall not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating national competent authority and the deployer
Holder (A): National competent authorities and the Commission
Holder (B): National competent authorities and the Commission

Note (A): Applies when Annex III point 1, 6 or 7 systems are used by law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities and disclosure would jeopardise public and national security. The deployer here is a public authority with a consultation right. Exchange 'shall not cover sensitive operational data'.
Note (B): Public-sector rule: applies when Annex III points 1, 6 or 7 systems are used by law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities and disclosure 'would jeopardise public and national security interests'. Exchange excludes their sensitive operational data.

Quote (A): Those authorities shall ensure that the market surveillance authorities referred to in Article 74(8) and (9), as applicable, can, upon request, immediately access the documentation or obtain a copy thereof.
Quote (B): Those authorities shall ensure that the market surveillance authorities referred to in Article 74(8) and (9), as applicable, can, upon request, immediately access the documentation or obtain a copy thereof.
