Holder (B): Law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities that are providers of Annex III point 1, 6 or 7 high-risk AI systems
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Public authorities as providers answer to their market surveillance authority. The technical documentation 'shall remain within the premises of those authorities'; 'Only staff of the market surveillance authority holding the appropriate level of security clearance shall be allowed to access'.
Note (B): Public bodies as providers: Annex IV technical documentation 'shall remain within the premises of those authorities'; they answer to the MSA on request. 'Only staff of the market surveillance authority holding the appropriate level of security clearance' may access it.

Quote (A): Where risks to fundamental rights are identified, the market surveillance authority shall also inform and fully cooperate with the relevant national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).
Quote (B): Where risks to fundamental rights are identified, the market surveillance authority shall also inform and fully cooperate with the relevant national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1).
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Link to fundamental-rights bodies.
Note (B): Link between market surveillance and fundamental rights bodies.

Quote (A): it shall without undue delay require the relevant operator to take all appropriate corrective actions to bring the AI system into compliance, to withdraw the AI system from the market, or to recall it
Quote (B): it shall without undue delay require the relevant operator to take all appropriate corrective actions to bring the AI system into compliance, to withdraw the AI system from the market, or to recall it
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Authority to require correction, withdrawal or recall. Trigger: evaluation finds non-compliance. Period: as prescribed, 'in any event within the shorter of 15 working days' or as in harmonisation legislation. Notified body informed; Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies. [inference] 'Operator' can include a public-sector deployer.
Note (B): Authority to require correction, withdrawal or recall. Trigger: evaluation finds non-compliance. Deadline: period the MSA prescribes, at most 15 working days or as sectoral law provides. MSA informs the notified body. Operators include deployers [inference from 'operator'; definition is in Art. 3].

Quote (A): The operator shall ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market.
Quote (B): The operator shall ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market.
Position (A): public or private (operators include providers and deployers)
If not met (A): provisional measures to prohibit, restrict, withdraw or recall (Art. 79(5))
Note (A): Corrective action carried out by the operator.
Note (B): Corrective action carried out by the operator itself.

Quote (A): the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the AI system’s being made available on its national market or put into service
Quote (B): the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the AI system’s being made available on its national market or put into service
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Authority to stop or restrict, or withdraw or recall. Trigger: operator fails to take adequate corrective action in the period. The notification (Art. 79(6)) must say whether non-compliance stems from Art. 5 prohibitions, Chapter III Section 2 requirements, shortcomings in harmonised standards or common specifications, or Art. 50.
Note (B): Authority to stop a tool. Trigger: operator does not take adequate corrective action in time. Also withdrawal or recall.

Quote (A): That authority shall without undue delay notify the Commission and the other Member States of those measures.
Quote (B): That authority shall without undue delay notify the Commission and the other Member States of those measures.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Notification content: identification of the system, origin and supply chain, nature of non-compliance and risk, national measures, and the operator's arguments (Art. 79(6)).
Note (B): Notification content (79(6)) includes whether non-compliance is due to Art. 5 prohibitions, Chapter III Section 2 failures, shortcomings in harmonised standards, or Art. 50. 79(3): inform when non-compliance is not limited to the national territory. 79(7): other MSAs report measures and objections.

Quote (A): The market surveillance authorities shall ensure that appropriate restrictive measures are taken in respect of the product or the AI system concerned, such as withdrawal of the product or the AI system from their market, without undue delay.
Quote (B): The market surveillance authorities shall ensure that appropriate restrictive measures are taken in respect of the product or the AI system concerned, such as withdrawal of the product or the AI system from their market, without undue delay.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Union-wide effect. Art. 79(8): a provisional measure is 'deemed justified' if no objection within three months (30 days for Art. 5 breaches), without prejudice to the operator's procedural rights.
Note (B): 79(8): a provisional measure with no objection within three months (30 days for Art. 5 cases) 'shall be deemed justified'.

Quote (A): it shall without undue delay require the relevant provider to take all necessary actions to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation
Quote (B): it shall without undue delay require the relevant provider to take all necessary actions to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Reclassification as high-risk. Also requires corrective action within a prescribed period. If use extends beyond national territory, the authority informs the Commission and other Member States (Art. 80(3)).
Note (B): Trigger: evaluation finds the system is high-risk. 80(3): inform Commission and Member States if use is not limited to national territory. 80(5): provider ensures corrective action for all systems concerned.

Quote (A): the AI system was misclassified by the provider as non-high-risk in order to circumvent the application of requirements in Chapter III, Section 2, the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99
Quote (B): the AI system was misclassified by the provider as non-high-risk in order to circumvent the application of requirements in Chapter III, Section 2, the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99.
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (providers may also be public authorities)
Note (A): Sanction for deliberate misclassification, established by the market surveillance authority during evaluation.
Note (B): Sanction for deliberate misclassification, established in the MSA's evaluation.

Quote (A): The provider or other relevant operator shall ensure that corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market within the timeline prescribed
Quote (B): The provider or other relevant operator shall ensure that corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned that it has made available on the Union market
Holder (A): The provider or other relevant operator
Holder (B): The provider or other relevant operator
Position (A): public or private (operators include providers and deployers)
Note (A): Corrective action within the authority's timeline.
Note (B): Within the timeline the MSA prescribes.

Quote (A): the Commission shall decide whether the measure is justified and, where necessary, propose other appropriate measures.
Quote (B): On the basis of the results of that evaluation, the Commission shall decide whether the measure is justified and, where necessary, propose other appropriate measures.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): After consulting the Member States and operators and evaluating the national measures. Member States must 'immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States' of a finding (Art. 82(3)); the Commission communicates its decision (Art. 82(5)).
Note (B): After consulting Member States and operators. 82(5): decision communicated immediately to Member States and operators.

Quote (A): any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority.
Quote (B): any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority.
Holder (A): Any natural or legal person (complainant); market surveillance authority (receives)
Holder (B): Any natural or legal person (right); relevant market surveillance authority (receives complaints)
Position (A): outside the state: any natural or legal person
Note (A): Complaint route, 'Without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies'. Complaints 'shall be taken into account for the purpose of conducting market surveillance activities' and handled under the authorities' own procedures. [inference] No right to a decision on the complaint is stated.
Note (B): Complaint route, 'without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies'. Complaints 'shall be taken into account for the purpose of conducting market surveillance activities'; no outcome or individual remedy stated. Covers complaints about public-sector AI [inference].

Quote (A): shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
Quote (B): shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
Position (A): deployers include public authorities (e.g. Annex III points 5(a), 6, 7) [inference]; affected persons outside the state
If not met (A): not stated in this Article; [inference] complaint to the market surveillance authority (Art. 85). Art. 86 is not among the provisions listed for fines in Art. 99(4).
Note (A): Right to explanation. Applies to decisions 'taken by the deployer on the basis of the output from a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, with the exception of systems listed under point 2', with legal or similarly significant adverse effects on health, safety or fundamental rights. Exceptions from Union or national law (Art. 86(2)); applies only where not otherwise provided under Union law (Art. 86(3)).
Note (B): Deployer answers to the affected person. Trigger: decision by the deployer based on output of an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2) with legal or similarly significant adverse effects on health, safety or fundamental rights. Exceptions under Union or national law (86(2)); applies only if not otherwise provided in Union law (86(3)). Relevant to public deployers, e.g. Annex III 5(a) benefits.

Quote (A): Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
Quote (B): Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
Position (A): not stated
Note (A): Whistleblowing route; points to another instrument. Nearest named actors: persons reporting infringements.
Note (B): Whistleblowing route and protection; details in Directive 2019/1937, outside this document.

Quote (A): The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94.
Quote (B): The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94.
Holder (A): Commission (implementation entrusted to the AI Office)
Holder (B): The Commission (entrusted to the AI Office)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Assigns authority over general-purpose AI model obligations (Chapter V, outside this part). 'The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office'.
Note (B): Allocates authority over general-purpose AI model providers to the EU level. 'The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office.' Also Accountability in effect (providers answer to the Commission).

Quote (A): market surveillance authorities may request the Commission to exercise the powers laid down in this Section, where that is necessary and proportionate to assist with the fulfilment of their tasks under this Regulation.
Quote (B): market surveillance authorities may request the Commission to exercise the powers laid down in this Section, where that is necessary and proportionate to assist with the fulfilment of their tasks under this Regulation.
Position (A): public authority: Member State authority
Note (A): Referral from national to EU level; without prejudice to Art. 75(3).
Note (B): Referral from national to EU level.

Quote (A): the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models, including their adherence to approved codes of practice.
Quote (B): the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models, including their adherence to approved codes of practice.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (AI Office, within the Commission)
Note (A): General-purpose model providers answer to the AI Office.
Note (B): General-purpose AI model providers answer to the AI Office. Consequence: Arts 91-93 powers and Art. 101 fines.

Quote (A): Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation.
Quote (B): Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation.
Position (A): outside the state: private companies, or public bodies building AI systems on a general-purpose model [inference]
Note (A): Complaint route against model providers. Must be 'duly reasoned' and state the model provider's contact point, the facts, provisions concerned and reasons. The body receiving it is not named in Art. 89(2) [inference: the AI Office].
Note (B): Complaint route against general-purpose AI model providers. Must be 'duly reasoned' with the provider's contact point, facts and provisions concerned. Public bodies building systems on such models could be downstream providers [inference].

Quote (A): The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that:
Quote (B): The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that
Position (A): outside the state: independent experts (selected by the Commission)
Note (A): Alert mechanism: (a) a model 'poses concrete identifiable risk at Union level', or (b) meets Art. 51 conditions. Note (B): Referral. Grounds: a model 'poses concrete identifiable risk at Union level' or meets Art. 51 conditions. 90(2): the Commission may then use its Section 5 powers after informing the Board; AI Office informs the Board of measures. Alert must be duly reasoned (90(3)).

Quote (A): The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55, or any additional information
Quote (B): The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55
Holder (A): Commission (requests); provider of the general-purpose AI model (supplies)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution; outside the state: private companies
Level of obligation (A): statutory power (Commission); statutory duty (provider must supply)
If not met (A): fines under Art. 101 'for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information' (Art. 91(4); Art. 101(1)(b))
Note (A): A structured dialogue may precede (Art. 91(2)); may be triggered by the scientific panel (Art. 91(3)). Request states legal basis, purpose and deadline. Clients 'remain fully responsible if the information supplied is incomplete, incorrect or misleading' (Art. 91(5)).
Note (B): Information power over model providers, 'or any additional information that is necessary'. AI Office may first open a 'structured dialogue' (91(2)); request may follow a scientific panel request (91(3)). Request must state legal basis, purpose, period and fines (91(4)).

Quote (A): the Commission may request access to the general-purpose AI model concerned through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code.
Quote (B): the Commission may request access to the general-purpose AI model concerned through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code.
Holder (A): Commission (requests access); providers of the general-purpose AI model (provide it)
Holder (B): The Commission; providers of the general-purpose AI model
Position (A): public authority: EU institution; outside the state: private companies
Level of obligation (A): statutory power (Commission); statutory duty (provider must give access)
If not met (A): 'the fines provided for in Article 101 for failure to provide access' (Art. 92(4); Art. 101(1)(d))
Note (A): Before requesting access, the AI Office may hold a structured dialogue on 'the internal testing of the model, internal safeguards for preventing systemic risks, and other internal procedures' (Art. 92(7)).
Note (B): Audit access. Providers 'shall provide the access requested' (92(5)).

Quote (A): restrict the making available on the market, withdraw or recall the model.
Quote (B): restrict the making available on the market, withdraw or recall the model
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
If not met (A): fines for failing to comply with a requested measure (Art. 101(1)(c))
Note (A): Authority over general-purpose models: may also request (a) measures to comply with Arts. 53-54, (b) mitigation where an Art. 92 evaluation gives 'serious and substantiated concern of a systemic risk at Union level'. A structured dialogue may precede; the Commission 'may, by decision, make those commitments binding' (Art. 93(3)).
Note (B): 'Where necessary and appropriate, the Commission may request providers to' comply with Arts 53-54, (b) implement mitigation after an Art. 92 evaluation raises 'serious and substantiated concern of a systemic risk', or (c) restrict, withdraw or recall.

Quote (A): Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model
Quote (B): Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model
Holder (B): Providers of the general-purpose AI model
Position (A): outside the state: private companies
Note (A): Challenge route for model providers; points to another instrument whose content is not set out here.
Note (B): Procedural rights against Commission enforcement; content is in Regulation 2019/1020 Art. 18, outside this document [inference: includes a right to be heard and remedies].

Quote (A): The AI Office and the Member States shall facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct concerning the voluntary application, including by deployers, of specific requirements to all AI systems
Quote (B): The AI Office and the Member States shall facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct concerning the voluntary application, including by deployers, of specific requirements to all AI systems
Holder (A): AI Office and the Member States
Holder (B): The AI Office and the Member States
Position (A): public authority: EU institution; public authority: Member State
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty (AI Office and Member States); voluntary for code authors
Note (A): Codes 'on the basis of clear objectives and key performance indicators'. Elements include Union ethical guidelines for trustworthy AI; environmental impact; AI literacy; inclusive design and diverse teams with stakeholder participation; 'assessing and preventing the negative impact of AI systems on vulnerable persons', accessibility and gender equality.
Note (B): Support for voluntary standard-setting (serves 95(3)). Codes to have 'clear objectives and key performance indicators', e.g. ethics guidelines, environmental impact, AI literacy, inclusive design, impact on vulnerable persons. 95(1): codes for voluntary application of Chapter III Section 2 to non-high-risk systems. 95(4): account for SMEs.

Quote (A): Codes of conduct may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers of AI systems or by organisations representing them or by both
Quote (B): Codes of conduct may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers of AI systems or by organisations representing them or by both
Holder (A): Individual providers or deployers of AI systems, or organisations representing them
Holder (B): Individual providers or deployers of AI systems, or organisations representing them
Position (A): public or private (deployers include public bodies)
Note (A): Voluntary self-set standards, possibly with stakeholders 'including civil society organisations and academia'. [inference] A public-sector deployer could adopt its own code.
Note (B): Voluntary standard-setting, 'including with the involvement of any interested stakeholders ... including civil society organisations and academia'. Public deployers could adopt codes [inference].

Quote (A): The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
Quote (B): The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Covers delegated acts under Arts. 6(6)-(7), 7(1) and (3), 11(3), 43(5)-(6), 47(5), 51(3), 52(4), 53(5)-(6) [inference: including amending Annex III and the high-risk classification conditions]. Five years from 1 August 2024, tacitly extended. Also coded Accountability/Design.
Note (B): Covers powers in Arts 6(6)-(7), 7(1) and (3) (changes to the high-risk list), 11(3), 43(5)-(6), 47(5), 51(3), 52(4), 53(5)-(6), for five years from 1 August 2024, tacitly extended. Authority to change scope.

Quote (A): The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
Quote (B): The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Examination procedure (Art. 5 Regulation (EU) No 182/2011) applies to implementing acts, e.g. those under Arts. 58, 60, 68, 72, 92, 101. [inference] The committee of Member State representatives also controls those acts [could be read as Decision-making].
Note (B): Comitology for implementing acts (examination procedure, Art. 5 of Regulation 182/2011). Under that Regulation the committee's opinion can block an act [inference; outside this document], so this may also be read as Decision-making.

Quote (A): Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include warnings and non-monetary measures, applicable to infringements of this Regulation by operators
Quote (B): Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include warnings and non-monetary measures, applicable to infringements of this Regulation by operators
Position (A): public authority: Member State
Note (A): Sanctions regime. Penalties 'shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive' and take SMEs into account; Commission guidelines (Art. 96) to be considered. Member States notify the rules to the Commission by the date of application (Art. 99(2)). Fines may be imposed by courts or other bodies depending on the legal system (Art. 99(9)).
Note (B): Sanctions regime. 'The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.' Take account of Commission guidelines and SMEs. Notify the Commission of the rules (99(2)).

Quote (A): Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines
Quote (B): Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines
Position (A): public or private (operators include public-sector deployers; see Art. 99(8))
If not met (A): administrative fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
Note (A): Answer to: the authority imposing fines under national rules. SMEs: the lower of the amount or percentage (Art. 99(6)). Quote stops before the amounts to avoid spacing errors in the figures.
Note (B): Fine amounts given in the note to avoid special spacing characters in the quote. For public authorities, see Art. 99(8).

Quote (A): Non-compliance with any of the following provisions related to operators or notified bodies, other than those laid down in Articles 5, shall be subject to administrative fines
Quote (B): Non-compliance with any of the following provisions related to operators or notified bodies, other than those laid down in Articles 5, shall be subject to administrative fines
Holder (A): Providers, authorised representatives, importers, distributors, deployers, notified bodies
Position (A): public or private (deployers include public bodies; see Art. 99(8))
If not met (A): administrative fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
Note (A): Listed: (a) providers, Art. 16; (b) authorised representatives, Art. 22; (c) importers, Art. 23; (d) distributors, Art. 24; '(e) obligations of deployers pursuant to Article 26'; (f) notified bodies, Arts. 31, 33(1), (3), (4), 34; (g) transparency for providers and deployers, Art. 50. Note (B): Listed: (a) providers' obligations under Art. 16; (b) authorised representatives Art. 22; (c) importers Art. 23; (d) distributors Art. 24; (e) deployers Art. 26 (coded separately); (f) notified bodies Arts 31, 33, 34; (g) Art. 50 transparency for providers and deployers.

Quote (A): The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines
Quote (B): The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines
Holder (B): Operators and others replying to requests (offenders)
Position (A): not stated
If not met (A): administrative fines up to EUR 7 500 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 1% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
Note (A): Answerability for information given to supervisors. Nearest named actors: operators replying to requests.

Quote (A): For the purpose of determining that a general-purpose AI model has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in Article 51(1), point (a), the Commission shall take into account the following criteria:
Quote (B): For the purpose of determining that a general-purpose AI model has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in Article 51(1), point (a), the Commission shall take into account the following criteria

Note (A): Criteria: parameters; data set size; training compute; modalities; benchmarks and evaluations, including autonomy, scalability and tool access; reach, presumed high when made available to at least 10 000 registered business users in the Union; registered end-users. Decides which models carry systemic-risk obligations.
Note (B): Criteria for designating systemic-risk models: parameters, data size, training compute, modalities, benchmarks and evaluations, reach (presumed at 10,000 registered EU business users), number of registered end-users.

Quote (A): In light of the risks identified, deployers should determine measures to be taken in the case of a materialisation of those risks, including for example governance arrangements in that specific context of use
Quote (B): deployers should determine measures to be taken in the case of a materialisation of those risks, including for example governance arrangements in that specific context of use, such as arrangements for human oversight

Note (B): Authority to set governance arrangements for the context of use. Also coded Accountability (complaint handling and redress).

Quote (A): its capabilities and limitations in performance, including the degrees of accuracy for specific persons or groups of persons on which the system is intended to be used and the overall expected level of accuracy
Quote (B): the degrees of accuracy for specific persons or groups of persons on which the system is intended to be used and the overall expected level of accuracy in relation to its intended purpose
Position (A): not stated

Note (A): Records performance limits by group, foreseeable unintended outcomes and risks to health, safety, fundamental rights and discrimination, oversight measures, and input-data specifications. Nearest named actor: the provider.
Note (B): Metric: accuracy, overall and by group. Also foreseeable unintended outcomes and risks to health, safety, fundamental rights and discrimination. Point 4: 'appropriateness of the performance metrics'. Nearest named actor: provider.

Quote (A): the Commission shall take into account the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation.
Quote (B): the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account

Statutory (A): statutory: AI Act Art. 105 (amending Directive 2014/90/EU, Art. 8)
Note (A): Marine equipment: applies when the Commission carries out its activities and adopts technical specifications and testing standards for AI safety components. Public-sector link weak [coder judgement].
Note (B): Standard-setting: when adopting technical specifications and approval procedures for aviation security equipment concerning AI systems. Nearest actor: the Commission (named in the same formula in Art. 105). Same formula in Arts 103-109 for agricultural vehicles, two- or three-wheel vehicles, marine equipment, rail, motor vehicles, civil aviation and vehicle general safety; coded once. Quote (A): in particular when AI systems are used in the public sector, could involve relevant stakeholders, including the representatives of groups of persons likely to be affected by the AI system, independent experts, and civil society organisations
Quote (B): deployers of high-risk AI system, in particular when AI systems are used in the public sector, could involve relevant stakeholders, including the representatives of groups of persons likely to be affected by the AI system

Note (B): Also independent experts and civil society organisations, for the FRIA and for designing measures.

Quote (A): AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on its behalf to assist judicial authorities in researching and interpreting facts and the law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts.
Quote (B): it is appropriate to qualify as high-risk AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on its behalf to assist judicial authorities in researching and interpreting facts and the law

Note (B): Also ADR bodies when outcomes produce legal effects. Excludes 'purely ancillary administrative activities' (anonymisation, communication between personnel, administrative tasks).

Quote (A): the former provider should nonetheless closely cooperate and make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance

Note (B): Information, technical access and assistance provided to the new provider (who may be a public deployer turned provider under 25(1)), to fulfil Regulation obligations, 'in particular regarding the compliance with the conformity assessment'. Exception: where the initial provider 'has clearly specified that its AI system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system'. Without prejudice to IP rights, confidential business information and trade secrets (25(5)). Also coded Coordination/Design.

Quote (A): shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months

Note (B): Recording: 'for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data'. Financial institutions keep logs within financial-services documentation.

Quote (A): By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate and report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the following:
Quote (B): By 2 August 2029 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall submit a report on the evaluation and review of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council.

Note (B): Answer to: Parliament and Council. Includes 'the structure of enforcement and the possible need for a Union agency'; 'The reports shall be made public.' Related: 112(2) four-yearly reports on Annex III, Art. 50 and 'the supervision and governance system'; 112(4)(a) resources of NCAs; 112(4)(b) penalties; 112(13) enforcement assessment by 2 August 2031 (also to the EESC).

Quote (A): applies to the high-risk AI systems that have been placed on the market or put into service before the general date of application thereof, only if, from that date, those systems are subject to significant changes

Note (B): Scope: existing high-risk systems (other than Annex X systems) are covered only after significant design changes. Limited for public-sector systems by the next sentence (coded Delivery/Design). Set by the Regulation itself.

Quote (A): the power to adopt acts in accordance with Article 290 TFEU should be delegated to the Commission to amend the conditions under which an AI system is not to be considered to be high-risk
Quote (B): should be delegated to the Commission to amend the conditions under which an AI system is not to be considered to be high-risk, the list of high-risk AI systems

Commission to consult, including at expert level; 'the European Parliament and the Council receive all documents at the same time as Member States’ experts' (an accountability check on the delegated power). Operative provision Art. 97 (outside this part).

Quote (A): AI-generated or manipulated text to the extent it is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest unless the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control
Quote (B): a similar disclosure obligation in relation to AI-generated or manipulated text to the extent it is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a disclosure obligation
Note (A): Disclosure of AI-generated text published to inform the public, unless it has had human review or editorial control 'and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication'. Bears directly on public bodies publishing AI-drafted public information and on human review of AI outputs [inference]. Nearest named actor: deployers.
Note (B): Nearest actor: deployers (same recital) [inference]. Exception: 'unless the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility'. Bears on public bodies publishing AI-generated public information [inference].

Quote (A): should be authorised only if the relevant law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment and, unless provided otherwise in this Regulation, has registered the system in the database
Quote (B): shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment as provided for in Article 27 and has registered the system in the EU database according to Article 49

Note (A): Registration in the EU database 'as set out in this Regulation' as a condition of authorised use. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (FRIA, same quote). See Recital (131) on the non-public section for law enforcement.
Note (B): Registration in the EU database before use. 'However, in duly justified cases of urgency, the use of such systems may be commenced without the registration in the EU database, provided that such registration is completed without undue delay.' Law-enforcement registrations go to a secure non-public section (Art. 49(4)). Also coded Delivery/Design.

Quote (A): The use of the ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment as provided for in Article 27
Quote (B): shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment as provided for in Article 27 and has registered the system in the EU database according to Article 49
Position (A): public authority: member-state law enforcement
If not met (A): use is not to be authorised ('shall be authorised only if')
Note (A): Check: fundamental rights impact assessment (Art. 27); trigger: before use; compares against: not stated here; metric: not stated. Also coded Accountability/Design (registration).
Note (B): Impact assessment before use (trigger: before authorisation of real-time RBI use); content per Art. 27 (p. 69). Same passage also coded Accountability/Design (registration) and Decision-making/Design (approval condition).

Quote (A): The risk-management system should consist of a continuous, iterative process that is planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system.
Quote (B): The risk management system shall be understood as a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system, requiring regular systematic review and updating.
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Note (A): Recital (64) says the system is 'to be established by the provider' and measures should reflect 'the generally acknowledged state of the art'. Trigger: ongoing over the lifecycle, 'regularly reviewed and updated'; compared against: known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights in light of intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse; metric: not stated.
Note (B): Art. 9(1): 'A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained'. Nearest named actor: providers (Art. 9(9), Art. 16(a), Art. 17(1)(g)). Trigger: throughout lifecycle, regular review. Steps: identify known and reasonably foreseeable risks to 'health, safety or fundamental rights' under intended use; estimate risks incl. 'reasonably foreseeable misuse'; evaluate risks from post-market monitoring data (Art. 72); adopt targeted measures. Limited to risks that can be mitigated through development, design or technical information (9(3)).

Quote (A): has not been registered in the EU database referred to in Article 71, they shall not use that system and shall inform the provider or the distributor
Quote (B): When such deployers find that the high-risk AI system that they envisage using has not been registered in the EU database referred to in Article 71, they shall not use that system
Holder (A): such deployers (public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies)
Holder (B): such deployers (public authorities, or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies)
Position (A): public authority: member-state public authorities; EU institutions
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
Note (A): Gate: public-sector deployers must not use a high-risk system the provider has not registered. Trigger: before use ('envisage using').
Note (B): Use gate: public bodies must not use a high-risk system the provider has not registered. Trigger: before use. The informing element is a Coordination link to provider or distributor. Also coded Accountability/Design.

Quote (A): metrics used to measure accuracy, robustness and compliance with other relevant requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, as well as potentially discriminatory impacts
Quote (B): the validation and testing procedures used, including information about the validation and testing data used and their main characteristics; metrics used to measure accuracy, robustness and compliance with other relevant requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2
Position (A): not stated

Note (A): Validation and testing record. Trigger: development, and pre-determined changes (point 2(f)). Compared against: Chapter III, Section 2 requirements. Metrics: accuracy, robustness, potentially discriminatory impacts (specific metrics not prescribed). Also records validation and testing data and their characteristics. Also coded Accountability/Design (signed test reports).
Note (B): Testing record. Metrics: accuracy, robustness, compliance, 'as well as potentially discriminatory impacts'; includes pre-determined changes. Nearest named actor: provider. Also coded Accountability/Design (signed test reports).

Quote (A): High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models which are in conformity with harmonised standards or parts thereof the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union
Quote (B): which are in conformity with harmonised standards or parts thereof the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 shall be presumed to be in conformity
Holder (B): not stated (passive); nearest: European standardisation organisations (draft standards) and the Commission (publishes references)
Position (A): outside the state: European standardisation organisations [inference]
Level of obligation (A): statutory presumption of conformity (standards are a voluntary route)
Note (A): Such systems/models 'shall be presumed to be in conformity' with Section 2 or GPAI obligations to the extent covered. [inference] Whoever drafts the harmonised standard (European standardisation organisations, on Commission request, 40(2)) in effect sets what compliance means. Also coded Decision-making/Design (Commission requests).
Note (B): Standards become the practical yardstick for Section 2 requirements and GPAI obligations (Chapter V, Sections 2-3), 'to the extent that those standards cover those requirements or obligations'. Whoever sets the standard is Decision-making.

Quote (A): the Commission shall decide whether the authorisation is justified. The Commission shall address its decision to the Member State concerned and to the relevant operators.
Quote (B): decide whether the national measure is justified and shall notify its decision to the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
If not met (A): Authorisation withdrawn by the MSA if the Commission considers it unjustified (Art. 46(6)).
Note (A): Trigger: objection by a Member State within 15 days, or Commission considers authorisation contrary to Union law or unfounded; operators consulted. 46(7): for Annex I Section A products only sectoral derogations apply.
Note (B): Union safeguard procedure. Trigger: objection by another MSA, or Commission view that the measure is contrary to Union law. Deadline: six months (60 days for Art. 5 cases) from the Art. 79(5) notification, after consulting the MSA and operators.

Quote (A): AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels;
Quote (B): AI systems used in education or vocational training, in particular for determining access or admission, for assigning persons to educational and vocational training institutions or programmes at all levels, for evaluating learning outcomes of persons
Holder (B): European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
Position (A): not stated
Statutory (A): statutory: AI Act Annex III, point 3 (via Art. 6(2))
Note (A): Education: also (b) evaluating learning outcomes, (c) assessing the level of education a person will receive, (d) monitoring prohibited behaviour during tests. [inference] Covers public schools and universities.
Note (B): These 'should be classified as high-risk AI systems'; also assessing level of education and proctoring of tests. Covers public education bodies as deployers [inference].

Quote (A): They should serve as practical guidance to assist competent authorities under the AI Act in their enforcement activities, as well as providers and deployers of AI systems in ensuring compliance with their obligations under the AI Act
Quote (B): providers and deployers of AI systems in ensuring compliance with their obligations under the AI Act

Holder (B): European Commission (provides); providers and deployers of AI systems (recipients)

Note (A): Resource provided by a named actor (Commission) to serve providers' and deployers' compliance with Art. 5 (the Delivery and Decision-making design entries in this file). Also coded as Accountability/Resources (same passage, for competent authorities) and Coordination/Resources.
Note (B): Verb: should serve as practical guidance to assist. Serves the Delivery/Design entries in this document (compliance measures by providers and deployers). Non-binding (para 5). Also coded as Accountability/Resources and Coordination/Resources.

Quote (A): They should serve as practical guidance to assist competent authorities under the AI Act in their enforcement activities, as well as providers and deployers of AI systems in ensuring compliance with their obligations under the AI Act
Quote (B): practical guidance to assist competent authorities under the AI Act in their enforcement activities
Holder (A): European Commission (provider of the guidance); recipients: competent authorities under the AI Act
Holder (B): European Commission (provides); competent authorities under the AI Act (recipients)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Statutory (A): non-statutory: Commission guidelines adopted pursuant to AI Act Art. 96(1)(b) (para 3); non-binding (para 5)
Note (A): Resource provided by the Commission to serve enforcement by competent authorities (market surveillance authorities and the EDPS, para 53; see Accountability/Design entries). Also coded as Delivery/Resources (same passage) and Coordination/Resources.
Note (B): Verb: should serve as. The Guidelines themselves are the resource, serving enforcement of Art. 5 by market surveillance authorities (Accountability/Design entries, paras 53-56). Non-binding; authoritative interpretation only by the CJEU (para 5). Examples are merely indicative (para 7). Also coded as Delivery/Resources (providers and deployers) and Coordination/Resources (harmonised application, para 54).

Quote (A): These Guidelines will be regularly reviewed in light of the experience gained from the practical implementation of Article 5 AI Act and technological and market developments.
Quote (B): These Guidelines will be regularly reviewed in light of the experience gained from the practical implementation of Article 5 AI Act
Position (A): not stated
Statutory (A): non-statutory: Commission guidelines (stated commitment); guidelines adopted under AI Act Art. 96(1)(b)
Note (A): Passive: reviewer not named; nearest named actor is the European Commission (author). Coded as Decision-making because revising the guidance resets the official interpretation. Trigger: experience from practical implementation, technological and market developments; frequency 'regularly', not specified. Section 12 'Review and update of the Commission guidelines' falls in part 2. The same paragraph reports that the drafting was informed by a stakeholder consultation and that Member States in the AI Board and the European Parliament were consulted (report of process, not coded).
Note (B): Passive; nearest named actor is the Commission, which organised the consultation and drafted the Guidelines. Trigger: experience from practical implementation and technological and market developments; no interval stated. Coded as Decision-making because revising the interpretation sets the standard [inference]. Section 12 'Review and update of the Commission guidelines' falls in part 2. The consultation itself (stakeholders, Member States in the AI Board, European Parliament) is a report of what was done and is not coded.

Quote (A): The application of Article 5 AI Act will require a case-by-case assessment, which takes due account of the specific situation at issue in an individual case.
Quote (B): The application of Article 5 AI Act will require a case-by-case assessment, which takes due account of the specific situation at issue in an individual case.
Position (A): not stated
Statutory (A): non-statutory: Commission guidelines (non-binding interpretation of AI Act Art. 5)
Note (A): Passive: who carries out the assessment is not named; nearest named actors are competent authorities (enforcement) and providers and deployers (compliance), para 4. Check: trigger = each individual case; compares against = the cumulative conditions of each Art. 5 prohibition; metric = not stated. The paragraph adds that the examples in the Guidelines 'are merely indicative and are without prejudice to the need for such an assessment in each case'.
Note (B): Verb: will require. Nearest named actors: competent authorities, providers and deployers (para 4). Trigger: each individual case; compares against the cumulative conditions of each prohibition; metric not stated. The examples in the Guidelines are 'merely indicative and are without prejudice to the need for such an assessment in each case'. Case-by-case assessment is repeated for specific conditions at paras (88), (91), (164), (166), (167), (173).

Quote (A): Article 5 AI Act prohibits the placing on the EU market, putting into service, or use of certain AI systems for manipulative, exploitative , social control or surveillance practices
Quote (B): Article 5 AI Act prohibits the placing on the EU market, putting into service, or use of certain AI systems for manipulative, exploitative , social control or surveillance practices
Location (A): page 7 (printed p. 2), section 2, para (8); overview table para (9)
Holder (A): Providers and deployers of AI systems
Holder (B): Providers and deployers of AI systems
Position (A): mixed: public authority or outside the state: private companies (providers and deployers may be public authorities, agencies or private persons, paras 16-17)
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty (prohibition); applies from 2 February 2025 (para 3); restated in non-binding guidelines
If not met (A): Fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (para 55; AI Act Art. 99); for public authorities and bodies only if and to the extent national rules provide (para 55); EU institutions, bodies and agencies up to EUR 1 500 000 (para 55; AI Act Art. 100)
Note (A): General prohibition set by the EU legislature. Coded as Decision-making because it removes the provider's and deployer's discretion over whether such a tool may be placed on the market, put into service or used [inference]. Holder taken from para 15 (Guidelines focus on providers and deployers) and paras 62/150 (prohibitions apply to both 'each within their respective responsibilities'). The overview table (para 9) lists Art. 5(1)(a)-(h); (a), (b) and (c) are coded separately from their body text in this part; the body sections for (d)-(h) fall in part 2. Para 11: the Art. 5(1)(h) real-time RBI prohibition 'only applies to their use'. Para 14: 'use' is to include any misuse, reasonably foreseeable or not. Cross-ref Accountability entries on penalties (para 55).
Note (B): Verb: prohibits. Overall prohibition; constrains the decision whether a tool may be placed on the market, put into service or used. The overview table at para (9) lists eight prohibitions, Art. 5(1)(a)-(h); (a), (b) and (c) are coded separately in this part; (d)-(h) fall in part 2. Prohibitions apply from 2 February 2025 (para 3). Para (15): the Guidelines focus only on providers and deployers. Para (11): for real-time RBI (Art. 5(1)(h)) only use is prohibited.

Quote (A): The Guidelines on the Definition of an AI system provide the Commission’s interpretation of that definition.
Quote (B): The Guidelines on the Definition of an AI system provide the Commission’s interpretation of that definition.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Statutory (A): non-statutory: Commission guidelines on the definition of an AI system (interpreting AI Act Art. 3(1))
Note (A): Official Commission resource that the document points to (mention, not reproduced) for deciding whether a tool is an 'AI system' and so within scope of Art. 5. Footnotes 5 and 9 also point to the Commission Notice 'The Blue Guide on the implementation of EU product rules 2022' (2022/C 247/01) for definitions of placing on the market and related terms.
Note (B): Pointer to a separate official Commission resource (mention; not reproduced here). Coded as Decision-making/Resources because it serves the scope determination of whether a tool is an 'AI system' and so within the prohibitions [inference]; it could equally be read as serving Delivery.

Quote (A): While providers of AI systems must consider the conditions of use which may be reasonably foreseen prior to placing their AI systems on the market (intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse 8)
Quote (B): providers of AI systems must consider the conditions of use which may be reasonably foreseen prior to placing their AI systems on the market
Position (A): mixed: public authority or outside the state: private companies (providers may be public authorities or private persons, para 16)
Statutory (A): statutory: AI Act (intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse, Art. 3(12)-(13) cited in fn 8), as stated in Commission guidelines
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty as stated in non-binding guidelines ('must consider')
Note (A): Check: trigger = before placing on the market; compares against = intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; metric = not stated. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry for deployers (same sentence).
Note (B): Verb: must consider. Trigger: before placing on the market. Compares against intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; metric not stated. Para (14) also says 'use' for Art. 5 includes any misuse, reasonably foreseeable or not. Paired with the deployer entry from the same sentence.

Quote (A): deployers remain responsible for taking the lawful conditions for the use of the system into account.
Quote (B): deployers remain responsible for taking the lawful conditions for the use of the system into account
Position (A): mixed: public authority or outside the state: private companies (deployers include public authorities and agencies, para 17)
Statutory (A): statutory: AI Act (deployer obligations; article not cited in passage), as stated in Commission guidelines
Level of obligation (A): statutory duty as stated in non-binding guidelines ('remain responsible')
Note (A): Trigger: during use [inference]; what the lawful conditions are is not specified here. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry for providers (same sentence) and Accountability/Design entry (para 14, deployer liable regardless of provider's terms of use).
Note (B): Verb: remain responsible. Trigger: during use (ongoing). Compares against the lawful conditions of use; metric not stated. Also bears on Accountability (deployer responsibility). The example in the same paragraph (employer using emotion recognition) is coded separately as Accountability/Design.

Quote (A): The prohibition applies to deployers regardless of whether the provider (the supplier of the system) has excluded such use in its contractual relationships with the deployer (the employer), i.e. in the terms of use.
Quote (B): The prohibition applies to deployers regardless of whether the provider (the supplier of the system) has excluded such use in its contractual relationships with the deployer
Position (A): mixed: public authority or outside the state: private companies
Statutory (A): statutory: AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) (example), as interpreted in Commission guidelines
If not met (A): Fines under AI Act Art. 99 (para 55) [inference: not stated in this passage]
Note (A): Allocates answerability to the deployer for prohibited use; the provider's contractual exclusion does not shift it. To whom: not stated in passage (market surveillance authorities enforce, para 53). Consequence: not stated in passage. Example concerns an employer inferring emotions at the workplace. Cross-ref Coordination/Design entry (para 40, providers to exclude prohibited use in terms of use).
Note (B): Responsibility for prohibited use stays with the deployer whatever the supply contract says. To whom: not stated (market surveillance authorities, para 53). The example concerns emotion recognition at the workplace (Art. 5(1)(f)); public bodies as employers would fall within it [inference]. Cross-reference Coordination/Design (providers' terms of use, para 40).

Quote (A): ‘Authority’ over an AI system  should be understood as assuming responsibility over the decision to deploy the system and over the manner of its actual use.
Quote (B): ‘Authority’ over an AI system  should be understood as assuming responsibility over the decision to deploy the system and over the manner of its actual use.
Holder (A): Deployers: natural or legal persons, public authorities, agencies or other bodies using AI systems under their authority
Holder (B): Deployers: natural or legal persons, public authorities, agencies or other bodies using AI systems under their authority
Position (A): mixed: public authority or outside the state: private companies
